stories.summary: Ukraine plans to establish its first civilian air defense groups at ports and railway facilities. Separately, a Russian attack killed a civilian on a commuter train in the city of Kharkiv.

stories.title: Reuters: 40% of Russia’s oil exports offline, mostly due to Ukrainian drone strikes — worst disruption in Russian history
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes have knocked approximately 40% of Russia's oil exports offline, halting oil loadings at both Russian Baltic Sea terminals. Reuters reported it as the worst disruption to Russian oil exports in the country's history.

stories.title: Lukashenko 'not an independent actor’: opposition leader Tsikhanouskaya on why Belarus needs Russia
stories.summary: Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya said President Alexander Lukashenko remains dependent on Russia despite recent diplomatic outreach, including U.S. negotiations and a visit to North Korea.

stories.title: Iran rejects US ceasefire plan, issues own demands as strikes land across the Middle East
stories.summary: Iran rejected an American ceasefire proposal and launched additional attacks on Israel and Gulf Arab states, including an assault that caused a major fire at Kuwait International Airport. Israel struck Tehran while the U.S. deployed paratroopers and Marines to the region.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz, Bilawal discuss regional situation, Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts for peace
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Wednesday to discuss the evolving Gulf situation amid the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. Sharif briefed Bilawal on Pakistan's diplomatic efforts to promote peace. Both leaders also discussed internal security challenges.

stories.title: UN designates slave trade as ‘gravest crime against humanity’ despite US opposition
stories.summary: The UN General Assembly designated the transatlantic African slave trade as "the gravest crime against humanity" in a vote advocates called a step toward reparations. The United States, Israel, and Argentina opposed the measure, while Britain and EU states abstained.

stories.title: German army eyes AI tools to expedite wartime decision-making
stories.summary: Germany's military is exploring AI tools to speed up decision-making during wartime. The German army commander said the Bundeswehr is drawing lessons from Ukrainian and other forces' experiences in current conflicts.

stories.title: The FSB ran ads offering Russians quick cash to commit sabotage. The agency called it a ‘social experiment.’
stories.summary: The Sverdlovsk branch of Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) posted Telegram advertisements offering 'easy money,' then asked respondents to carry out sabotage. The FSB described the operation as a 'social experiment.'

stories.title: Xi-Trump summit: White House locks in new dates in May, Beijing silent
stories.summary: The White House announced that a summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping will take place in Beijing on May 14–15. Trump said he would host Xi for a reciprocal visit in Washington later in the year.

stories.title: UN chief says ‘high time’ to end ‘out of control’ war on Iran
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for an end to the conflict involving Iran, describing the war in the Middle East as "out of control" and saying it is "high time" to stop it.

stories.title: Rosatom Pulls More Staff From Iranian Nuclear Plant After Reported Strike
stories.summary: Russia's state nuclear agency Rosatom has withdrawn additional staff from the Bushehr nuclear power plant in Iran following a reported strike. Iran's atomic energy organization said a projectile landed inside the plant's compound on Tuesday but caused no damage, blaming the US and Israel.

stories.title: UN chief names Arnault as personal envoy for Middle East war
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres appointed veteran French diplomat Jean Arnault as his personal envoy for the Middle East war. Arnault brings more than 30 years of experience in peace mediation from UN missions across Africa, Asia, and Europe.

stories.title: Centcom says more than 50,000 US troops now in region
stories.summary: US Central Command announced that more than 50,000 American troops are now deployed across the Middle East region, including approximately 200 combat aircraft, two aircraft carriers, and reinforcements from the 82nd Airborne Division and Marine Expeditionary Units.

stories.title: Iran’s state TV outlines five conditions to end war
stories.summary: Iranian state television outlined five conditions that must be met before Iran would agree to end the war with the US and Israel.

stories.title: UNESCO reacts to strike on Lviv city center but does not mention Russia
stories.summary: UNESCO expressed concern over a drone strike on the central part of Lviv, a UNESCO World Heritage site, but did not name Russia as the perpetrator in its statement.

stories.title: Sharif briefs Saudi Crown Prince as Pakistan pushes to mediate U.S.-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif briefed Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman as Pakistan seeks to mediate U.S.-Iran talks. Sharif condemned recent attacks on the Kingdom and reaffirmed Islamabad's solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Italy’s tourism minister resigns amid turmoil from referendum failure
stories.summary: Italy's Tourism Minister Daniela Santanchè resigned after Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni publicly asked her to step down. The move came as Meloni sought to restore government credibility following a defeat in a referendum on judicial reform.

stories.title: Turkey, UK sign training and support deal for multibillion-dollar Eurofighter order
stories.summary: Turkey and the United Kingdom signed a training and support agreement tied to Turkey's multibillion-dollar order of Eurofighter combat aircraft. The Turkish air force aims to eventually perform its own depot-level maintenance of the airframes, engines, and other equipment domestically.

stories.title: He Researched Public Health in the Arctic. Russia Says It Was Treason.
stories.summary: Russian authorities imprisoned a scientist on treason charges related to his public health research in the Arctic. The case has raised questions about the actual motivations behind the prosecution of the respected researcher.

stories.title: Hungary to curb gas flows to Ukraine until Druzhba oil flows resume, Orban says
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán announced that Hungary will gradually halt natural gas deliveries to Ukraine until crude oil flows on the Druzhba pipeline resume. The move escalates an energy standoff between Budapest and Kyiv over supplies disrupted by the war.

stories.title: Israel forcibly displaces more Palestinian families in East Jerusalem
stories.summary: Rights groups reported that Israel forcibly displaced additional Palestinian families in occupied East Jerusalem, describing the actions as an expansion of ethnic cleansing in the area.

stories.title: ‘Too early to tell’ if timeline holds for delivery of Army’s tilt-rotor MV-75 for testing: Official
stories.summary: A U.S. Army official said it is too early to determine whether the delivery timeline for the tilt-rotor MV-75 aircraft will hold. Maj. Gen. Clair Gill noted that risk decisions may be needed if system performance cannot keep pace with the schedule.

stories.title: Minnesota sues US govt over shootings by immigration agents
stories.summary: The U.S. state of Minnesota has filed a lawsuit against the federal government over shootings by immigration agents, accusing federal authorities of blocking access to evidence related to the incidents.

stories.title: Russia’s hypersonic Zircon missiles are hard to shoot down. So Ukraine is blasting them on the ground.
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone operators are targeting Russia's hypersonic Zircon missiles on the ground after degrading Russian air defenses in Crimea. The strategy aims to neutralize the hard-to-intercept missiles before launch.

stories.title: Memetic warfare: US, Iran, and Israel battle for meme dominance and social media virality
stories.summary: The United States, Iran, and Israel are engaged in a social media information war, deploying memes and viral content to influence public opinion. Governments are targeting younger audiences who increasingly consume news through social media platforms.

stories.title: Putin watched Khamenei get killed. Then disappeared from public view for nine days. Then shut down Moscow’s internet
stories.summary: Moscow's internet was shut down following the killing of Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei. Russian President Vladimir Putin reportedly disappeared from public view for nine days after witnessing the event.

stories.title: Israeli spyware maker to appeal conviction in Greece’s Predator case
stories.summary: Intellexa founder Tal Dilian announced he will appeal his eight-year prison sentence in Greece's Predator spyware case. Dilian was convicted for surveillance targeting politicians and journalists and said he refuses to serve as a scapegoat in the scandal.

stories.title: Mayor of Mechelen comes under Russian fire during visit to Lviv
stories.summary: A delegation from the Belgian city of Mechelen, delivering humanitarian aid including fire trucks and police vehicles to Lviv, was caught in a Russian strike on the city center on March 24.

stories.title: Why gold has fallen despite heightened global tensions
stories.summary: Gold prices have fallen sharply since the outbreak of the Middle East war, erasing most of 2026's gains despite the metal's traditional safe-haven status. Analysts attribute the decline to investors liquidating gold holdings to raise cash and offset losses in other assets amid rising economic uncertainty.

stories.title: IRGC commander warns Trump threats amount to ‘act of war’
stories.summary: IRGC Aerospace Force commander Majid Mousavi warned that US threats and ultimatums against Iran constitute an act of war. In a post on X, Mousavi cited recent strikes on Dimona and Haifa as a response to what he described as US threats regarding the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Iraq’s Kurdistan is becoming the new frontline in a widening Iran war
stories.summary: Iraq's Kurdistan region is emerging as a new frontline in the widening war involving Iran. Kurdish lawmakers in Baghdad have warned that the federal government's restrained response risks further destabilising the country.

stories.title: These pro-Palestine PACs are trying to beat AIPAC at its own game
stories.summary: Several pro-Palestine political action committees in the United States are working to counterbalance AIPAC's influence in elections. The efforts come as polling indicates declining American sympathy toward Israel.

stories.title: Iran rejects Trump's 15-point peace proposal with five conditions of its own
stories.summary: Iran rejected the US 15-point peace proposal and responded with five conditions of its own, according to Iranian state media. Tehran's demands include guarantees against future US-Israeli attacks, reparations, and control over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Hungarian election: Will Europe's far-right help Orban win?
stories.summary: Leading European far-right and populist figures are supporting Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's reelection campaign. However, Orbán trails the opposition amid allegations of corruption, scandal, and his ties to Russia.

stories.title: Iranian strikes pose ‘existential threat’, Gulf states tell UN
stories.summary: Gulf states have told the United Nations that Iranian strikes pose an "existential threat" to their countries. Tehran has defended its military actions, stating it is fighting an enemy that "will be beyond containment tomorrow."

stories.title: Iran targets US public opinion with online information war
stories.summary: Iran has been conducting an online influence campaign using AI-generated photos, videos, and memes to sow confusion about the Middle East war. Experts say the campaign's primary goal is to amplify anti-war sentiment in the United States and pressure President Trump to end the conflict.

stories.title: Jury finds Meta and Google liable for US$6 million damages in social media addiction trial
stories.summary: A jury found Meta liable for $4.2 million and Google for $1.8 million in damages for designing social media platforms deemed dangerous for children and teenagers. The landmark verdict could push tech companies to reconsider how they address youth safety claims.

stories.title: Russia says it remains in contact with US on Ukraine settlement
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on March 25 that Russia remains in contact with the United States regarding a possible settlement of the conflict in Ukraine. Moscow expressed hope that Washington would continue its mediation efforts.

stories.title: Despite Iran war, 40 American, Canadian Jews make aliyah ahead of Passover
stories.summary: Forty Jewish immigrants from the United States and Canada completed their aliyah to Israel ahead of Passover despite the ongoing war with Iran. Twenty-five arrived at Ben Gurion Airport while the remaining 15, already in Israel, finalized their immigration paperwork the same day.

stories.title: Trump Envoy Said Calling Europeans ‘Pussies’ Helped Win Lukashenko Over
stories.summary: US special envoy John Coale reportedly told others that calling Europeans 'pussies' helped him build rapport with Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko. Coale also admitted he did not know where Belarus was located when he was first approached for the diplomatic role.

stories.title: Israel’s 81% war consensus is an illusion - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis argues that Israel's reported 81% public consensus on the war is misleading. Disaggregated polling data reveals two distinct publics with markedly different understandings of the conflict's goals and meaning.

stories.title: Russia’s ballistic missiles now change trajectory mid-flight. Europe needs 400% increase in air defense or face defeat
stories.summary: Russia has developed ballistic missiles capable of changing trajectory mid-flight, reducing the effectiveness of Ukraine's Patriot interceptors and requiring multiple missiles per intercept. Analysts say Europe needs a 400% increase in air defense capacity to counter the threat.

stories.title: Russians strike hospital in Kharkiv region, injuring three
stories.summary: The Russian military shelled a hospital in the village of Shevchenkove in the Kupianskyi district of Ukraine's Kharkiv region. At least three people were injured according to preliminary reports.

stories.title: Russia evacuates more staff from Iran’s Bushehr nuclear plant
stories.summary: Russia's Rosatom evacuated another 163 staff from Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant, with about 300 personnel remaining on site. Construction of additional reactor units at the Russian-built facility has been suspended since the US-Israeli war on Iran began.

stories.title: Turkey relaying messages between Iran and US, says ruling party official
stories.summary: A Turkish ruling party official said Ankara is relaying messages between Iran and the United States amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. The official added that these communications were also being conveyed to Gulf nations, though no details of the messages were disclosed.

stories.title: Palestine Action hunger strikers to sue prisons over alleged mistreatment
stories.summary: Activists affiliated with Palestine Action who undertook hunger strikes while in UK custody announced plans to sue the prisons where they were held. The legal action alleges mistreatment during their detention in British prison facilities.

stories.title: Governments move to shield consumers from soaring energy costs
stories.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has driven oil prices up roughly 40% since the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, rattling global markets. Governments worldwide are now implementing measures to shield consumers from surging energy costs.

stories.title: Inside Trump’s quiet plan to ‘take’ Cuba
stories.summary: The United States continues to enforce a fuel blockade on Cuba even as international aid convoys attempt to reach the island. Reports describe a broader US strategy aimed at increasing pressure on the Cuban government.

stories.title: 230 students, teachers killed as US-Israel hit schools in Iran
stories.summary: Iran's Education Ministry reported that 230 students and teachers have been killed and over 600 educational and cultural facilities damaged since the start of the US-Israeli military campaign. The casualties resulted from strikes that hit schools across Iran.

stories.title: How the US plunged Cuba into darkness
stories.summary: A US-imposed oil blockade has pushed Cuba's power grid to the verge of total collapse. The fuel shortage has caused severe electricity disruptions across the island nation.

stories.title: Woman pleads not guilty to attempted murder of Rihanna and to assaulting singer’s family
stories.summary: Ivanna Lisette Ortiz, 35, of Orlando, Florida, pleaded not guilty in Los Angeles Superior Court to the attempted murder of singer Rihanna and over a dozen other felony counts. Prosecutors allege Ortiz fired shots at Rihanna's Beverly Hills-area home on March 8, targeting the singer, partner A$AP Rocky, and their three children.

stories.title: Ukraine Donor Platform meeting: PM Svyrydenko outlines reconstruction priorities to partners
stories.summary: The 16th meeting of the Ukraine Donor Platform Steering Committee took place in Kyiv. First Deputy Prime Minister Yuliia Svyrydenko outlined Ukraine's reconstruction priorities to international partners.

stories.title: Republicans propose bill to fund Iran war amid fight over DHS shutdown
stories.summary: Senate Republicans announced plans to use the reconciliation procedure to advance legislation that may fund the U.S. war with Iran and Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations. The effort, which could take weeks and faces no guarantee of success, comes amid a dispute over a Department of Homeland Security shutdown.

stories.title: Orbán threatened to cut gas supplies to Ukraine. This decision will cost $1 billion for Hungarian voters
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán threatened to cut gas supplies to Ukraine until transit of Russian oil via the Druzhba pipeline resumes. The decision is projected to cost Hungarian taxpayers approximately $1 billion.

stories.title: Veteran French diplomat as UN personal envoy for Middle East war
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres appointed veteran French diplomat Jean Arnault as his personal envoy for the Middle East war. The appointment aims to push peace efforts as the conflict risks wider escalation and threatens global oil, fertiliser, and food supplies.

stories.title: Iron from a 2,600-year-old shipwreck off Israeli coast may rewrite the history of war
stories.summary: Archaeologists discovered iron cargo from a 2,600-year-old shipwreck off the northern Israeli coast, providing the first evidence of iron being traded as a semifinished product. Researchers believe the material may have been destined for weapons production during an era of rivalry between ancient empires.

stories.title: 95th Brigade commander: Territorial concessions to freeze front line are unacceptable
stories.summary: Colonel Ruslan Maryshev, commander of Ukraine's 95th Polissia Separate Airborne Assault Brigade, stated that ceding territory in the Donetsk region to Russia in exchange for freezing the front line is unacceptable.

stories.title: How Are Iran’s Partnerships with Belarus and Russia Holding Up During War?
stories.summary: Analyst Jack Roush, who previously argued that the deepening Belarus-Iran security partnership could accelerate drone technology transfers to Russian forces in Ukraine, has revisited his findings in light of Iran's ongoing war with the United States and Israel. The partnership's implications for the Ukraine conflict remain a key concern.

stories.title: How Are Iran’s Partnerships with Belarus and Russia Holding Up During War?
stories.summary: An analysis revisits the security partnership between Belarus and Iran in light of the current U.S.-Israeli war against Iran. The piece examines how the deepening Belarus-Iran relationship could affect drone technology transfers to Russian forces fighting in Ukraine.

stories.title: Israeli strike damages home of Iranian director Abbas Kiarostami
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes in Tehran damaged the former home of acclaimed Iranian filmmaker Abbas Kiarostami. The incident has raised concerns about the destruction of cultural heritage sites during the ongoing military campaign.

stories.title: Israel urges UN to designate Hezbollah as ‘terrorist’ group
stories.summary: Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar called on the UN Security Council to designate Hezbollah a terrorist organization. Saar stated that Hezbollah has fired over 3,500 missiles, drones, and UAVs at Israel since Israel expanded its offensive on March 2.

stories.title: China shipping giant Cosco resumes bookings to some Gulf countries
stories.summary: Chinese shipping giant Cosco has resumed accepting bookings to certain Gulf countries, though it did not mention shipments traveling in the opposite direction from the Gulf. The move comes amid ongoing disruptions to maritime trade through the Strait of Hormuz due to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Israel evicts 11 Palestinian families in east Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israeli authorities evicted 11 Palestinian families in the Silwan neighborhood of East Jerusalem. The displacement has heightened tensions in the area, with clashes reported amid the broader regional conflict.

stories.title: FPV drone strikes in Baghdad expose US vulnerability
stories.summary: FPV drone strikes targeted locations in Baghdad, highlighting vulnerabilities in U.S. force protection. The attacks demonstrate that traditional fortifications are insufficient against cheap, persistent drone threats.

stories.title: Gavin Newsom says he regrets using the word ‘apartheid’ to describe Israel
stories.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom said he regrets using the word 'apartheid' to describe Israel. He stated his objections are directed at the current Israeli government rather than Israel as a state, though he did not say whether he considers himself a Zionist.

stories.title: War-linked power crunch pushes Sri Lanka to 4-day week
stories.summary: Sri Lanka shifted most state institutions, schools, and universities to a four-day working week on Wednesday to manage an energy crisis triggered by the Middle East war. Banks operated on reduced hours, and many private firms also curtailed operations as the country copes with a war-linked power shortage.

stories.title: 95th Brigade commander: Enemy tactics unchanged in Oleksandrivka sector
stories.summary: In the Oleksandrivka sector of the front line, Ukraine's 95th Polissia Separate Airborne Assault Brigade reports that its forces are dictating the terms of engagement. The brigade's commander noted that Russian enemy tactics in this area have remained unchanged.

stories.title: The Iran war and the uncertain future of the expats
stories.summary: The article examines how the ongoing war in the Gulf region is creating uncertainty for expatriate workers, particularly from India. While the Gulf remains economically significant for India, the conflict has undermined the longstanding appeal of the so-called Gulf dream.

stories.title: Denmark's Frederiksen faces tough coalition talks to remain prime minister
stories.summary: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen submitted her coalition government's resignation on Wednesday after a significant election defeat. She is expected to remain as caretaker leader and told supporters she was ready to lead a new government, with coalition negotiations now underway.

stories.title: Could Iran Actually Attack the U.S. Homeland With Drones?
stories.summary: Experts warn that no country is fully immune to the threat of drone warfare, amid discussion of whether Iran could potentially use drones to strike the U.S. homeland.

stories.title: Dutch opposition slams government: Financial aid to Ukraine nearly halved and far-right say “it’s not our war”
stories.summary: Dutch opposition lawmakers criticized the government after financial aid to Ukraine was nearly halved. Approximately €2 billion in previously approved aid remains delayed for unclear reasons, while far-right politicians argued the conflict is not the Netherlands' war.

stories.title: What we know about US attack on Iraqi military site
stories.summary: Iraqi authorities reported that a US air strike targeted a military site in Anbar province, killing seven Iraqi soldiers and wounding 13 others. The attack struck an established Iraqi military installation.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz tells authorities to expedite export of surplus food items to Gulf countries
stories.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed Pakistani authorities to accelerate exports of surplus food items to Gulf countries while maintaining domestic supply. He also called for expanded flight operations and improved port efficiency in response to the evolving regional situation in the Middle East.

stories.title: With eyes on trade deals and reform in global governance, Lula heads to India with 260 firms
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is visiting India accompanied by a delegation of 260 firms, the largest-ever Brazilian business delegation to the country. The trip focuses on trade deals and reform of global governance amid a challenging geopolitical environment.

stories.title: As two of the world’s largest democracies and dynamic economies, India and Brazil cannot remain distant: President Lula
stories.summary: Brazilian President Lula stated that India and Brazil, as two of the world's largest democracies, cannot remain distant from each other. He noted that bilateral trade reached its highest level in 2025 but remains far below its potential.

stories.title: BRICS shifts gears as Brazil passes the gavel to India amid global tensions and ambitious goals
stories.summary: Brazil is passing the BRICS presidency to India amid global tensions. Brazil's tenure was shaped by the aftereffects of multiple wars and U.S. tariffs, yet it advanced sustainability and inclusive development goals. India's presidency is expected to continue on a similar path.

stories.title: Turbulent South America builds up resistance to U.S.’s ‘Donroe doctrine’
stories.summary: Following the U.S. military's capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, South American nations are confronting a reassertion of Monroe Doctrine–style U.S. influence over the region. However, internal divisions among the continent's more than 450 million people are undermining efforts to form a united front.

stories.title: Israel's defence network challenged by Iranian cluster ballistic missiles
stories.summary: Iran has deployed cluster ballistic missiles against Israel, posing a new challenge to Israeli defense systems. Unlike single-warhead missiles, these weapons release hundreds of submunitions over civilian areas, creating lasting dangers similar to minefields after impact.

stories.title: Four arrested in Germany after  Channel smuggling gang raids
stories.summary: Four people were arrested in Germany following raids targeting a Channel smuggling gang. Europol said over 450 officers from the United Kingdom, Germany, and Belgium participated in the operation.

stories.title: Hezbollah chief rejects Israel talks as ‘surrender’ amid continued IDF strikes
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem rejected negotiations with Israel, characterizing them as surrender, and said fighters are prepared to continue operations without limits. The IDF continued strikes on Hezbollah headquarters, fuel networks, and operatives in Lebanon while rockets were fired at northern Israel.

stories.title: France says Gulf damage cuts oil supply by 11 million barrels a day
stories.summary: French Finance Minister Roland Lescure reported that 30 to 40 percent of Gulf refining capacity has been damaged or destroyed, removing 11 million barrels per day from global oil markets. He also noted that 17 percent of Qatar's gas production capacity was destroyed following attacks on energy facilities.

stories.title: With Bolsonaro in jail, Brazil’s right in disarray as Trump warms up to Lula
stories.summary: With former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro in jail, Brazil's political right is in disarray as his family faces a succession battle. Meanwhile, U.S. officials and markets signal waning support for the Bolsonaro brand, and President Trump has warmed relations with President Lula.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘Spear of the South’ sparks regional alarm as Venezuela braces for U.S. moves
stories.summary: Washington declared operation 'Spear of the South' targeting Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, described as a 'cartel head,' and has moved heavy firepower into the Caribbean. Observers say the operation may aim at regime change in Caracas and reasserting U.S. influence against growing Chinese and Russian presence in the region.

stories.title: After the gunfire: How Rio’s deadliest police raid exploded into a political battlefield
stories.summary: A deadly police raid in Rio de Janeiro has become a political flashpoint in Brazil. Rio's governor praised the operation as a victory against crime, but hundreds of favela residents marched carrying photos of the dead, calling it a massacre. President Lula's allies allege the raid was politically motivated.

stories.title: War-linked power crunch pushes Sri Lanka to four-day week
stories.summary: Sri Lanka has shifted most state institutions, schools, and universities to a four-day working week to cope with an energy crisis linked to the Middle East war. Banks in the country are operating on reduced hours, and private firms have also been affected by the power shortages.

stories.title: Trump’s boycott and Europe’s backslide may make BRICS lead climate debate and action at COP30
stories.summary: With President Trump boycotting COP30 and European climate commitments reportedly weakening, analysts suggest BRICS nations could take the lead on climate debate and action at the summit. Brazilian analysts believe the conference in Brazil will proceed effectively without Washington's participation.

stories.title: The US-Israel war on Iran has opened a regional Pandora’s box
stories.summary: Commentary by Muhannad Ayyash argues that the US-Israeli war on Iran has unleashed destabilizing forces across the Middle East. Competing visions for regime change in Iran risk prolonging regional instability.

stories.title: Sudan army-aligned governor accuses Ethiopia of backing RSF
stories.summary: A Sudanese military-aligned governor accused Ethiopia of supporting the Rapid Support Forces' offensive in Kurmuk. The escalating fighting has worsened displacement and deepened the humanitarian crisis in the region.

stories.title: India's historic haveli homes caught between revival and ruin
stories.summary: Historic haveli homes in Old Delhi, once grand residences of Mughal-era nobility, are caught between preservation and decay. While a handful have been restored, many more show cracked facades and sagging balconies, reflecting a heritage under growing threat.

stories.title: Casualties from Russian drone attack in Vinnytsia region rise to 21
stories.summary: Casualties from a Russian drone attack on March 24 in Ukraine's Vinnytsia region have risen to 21 injured. The strikes damaged 84 households across three communities in the region.

stories.title: ‘We want peace’: Iranians try to maintain semblance of normal life as conflict drags on
stories.summary: Residents of Tehran are attempting to maintain normal life despite ongoing Israeli airstrikes that have lit up the city's skyline. The conflict has disrupted the typically festive post-Nowruz period, with Iranians fearing the war could last weeks or months.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone pilots get round-the-clock support from another continent. While Kyiv sleeps, Australian experts run night shift
stories.summary: Australian experts are providing round-the-clock support to Ukrainian drone pilots by working aligned with Kyiv's time zone. The Australians run overnight shifts testing equipment and assisting pilots while Ukraine sleeps.

stories.title: NATO officer says allies must urgently rethink defence, prepare for 'new enemy'
stories.summary: NATO Supreme Allied Commander for Transformation Admiral Pierre Vandier urged allied nations at a Paris security forum to urgently rethink their defense posture. He said many countries have not grasped the scale of the challenge, particularly in boosting weapons production, emphasizing speed over funding as the key issue.

stories.title: British police arrest two men over arson attack on Jewish community ambulances
stories.summary: British police arrested two men in connection with an arson attack on four ambulances operated by a Jewish community organization in London. CCTV footage suggests at least three people were involved in the incident, and the investigation is ongoing.

stories.title: Iran rejects US 15-point peace plan, state media report
stories.summary: Iranian state media reported that Tehran has rejected a 15-point peace plan proposed by the United States. President Trump claimed he was in contact with key Iranian figures, but Iranian officials denied any such negotiations were taking place.

stories.title: United in fear, divided in politics – a view from Narva, an Estonian city bordering Russia
stories.summary: Narva, an Estonian city on the Russian border located 201 km from Tallinn, is home to roughly 53,000 residents, over 96 percent of whom are Russian speakers. The city's population navigates a complex political landscape shaped by proximity to Russia and membership in the European Union and NATO.

stories.title: Protest in India over cooking gas crisis
stories.summary: Indian opposition parties staged protests over a cooking gas shortage linked to the war on Iran. The conflict has disrupted energy supply chains, causing fuel shortages affecting Indian consumers.

stories.title: Cyprus begins talks with UK over future of British bases after Iranian drone strike
stories.summary: Cyprus has opened talks with the United Kingdom over the future of British military bases on the island following an Iranian drone strike. Cypriot officials expressed concern that the bases could expose the island to further attacks amid the ongoing war with Iran.

stories.title: Where do French parties stand a year before the presidential election?
stories.summary: With French local elections concluded, political parties are positioning ahead of the 2027 presidential election to succeed Emmanuel Macron. The left is divided over the Socialist Party's alliance with the radical-left France Unbowed, while the right debates whether to shift toward the center or align closer with Marine Le Pen's National Rally.

stories.title: Oops, we have wrecked another country
stories.summary: Former IAEA chief Mohammad ElBaradei warned that the US-Israeli war on Iran is not merely repeating past mistakes but amplifying them. The commentary draws parallels to previous conflicts while arguing the current situation carries even greater consequences.

stories.title: Stray Ukrainian drones hit Estonia, Latvia, including power station, officials say
stories.summary: Two stray Ukrainian military drones entered the airspace of Estonia and Latvia on March 25 after transiting through Russian airspace. One drone struck a chimney at a power station in one of the Baltic states, while the other crash-landed. Officials in both countries confirmed the incidents.

stories.title: Deadly US attack on Iraqi military base sparks condemnation
stories.summary: The United States carried out an air strike in Iraq targeting the Popular Mobilisation Forces, killing seven Iraqi soldiers. The attack has drawn widespread condemnation from Iraqi officials and other parties.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Israel expanding buffer zone in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that Israeli forces are expanding a buffer zone in southern Lebanon during ongoing operations against Hezbollah. Netanyahu said the zone aims to prevent infiltration toward the Galilee and push back anti-tank missile threats.

stories.title: Russian Energy Minister Confirms Oil Shipments to Cuba
stories.summary: Russian Energy Minister Sergei Tsivilev confirmed that Russia is shipping oil to Cuba, characterizing the deliveries as humanitarian aid and support.

stories.title: Netanyahu aide's racist slurs about Mizrahi Jews spark outrage
stories.summary: Leaked recordings revealed Netanyahu aide Ziv Agmon making racist remarks about Mizrahi Jews and criticizing Likud members of parliament. The recordings prompted widespread outrage and calls for Agmon's dismissal.

stories.title: Fire at Kuwait airport after drones hit fuel tank
stories.summary: Drones struck a fuel storage tank at Kuwait's airport, sparking a fire and disrupting flights. The attack occurred amid broader Iranian retaliatory strikes across the Gulf region as the war escalates.

stories.title: Denmark faces tough coalition talks following election
stories.summary: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen submitted her government's resignation after her three-party coalition suffered a major defeat in snap elections held on March 25. Neither the left nor right blocs won a parliamentary majority, leaving Frederiksen's future dependent on coalition talks with the centrist Moderate party led by Lars Løkke Rasmussen.

stories.title: Gaza toddler released from Israeli custody with ‘cigarette burn’ wounds
stories.summary: A 21-month-old Palestinian toddler named Jawad Abu Nassar was released from Israeli custody in Gaza bearing wounds his family described as cigarette burns. The family alleges the child shows signs of torture, while the toddler's father remains missing.

stories.title: Zelensky appoints heads of SSU counterintelligence and military counterintelligence departments
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky appointed Serhiy Hunkovsky as the new head of the Counterintelligence Department of the Security Service of Ukraine. The decree also included appointments to lead the military counterintelligence department.

stories.title: What it would take to end the Iran war
stories.summary: Analysis suggests that ending the US-Israeli war on Iran would require robust security guarantees and a credible international guarantor. The path to a ceasefire involves complex diplomatic conditions from both sides.

stories.title: Is war turning Tehran’s air into a chemical weapon?
stories.summary: US-Israeli strikes on oil facilities in Tehran have caused black rain containing toxic fallout to spread across the city. Residents face contamination of air, soil, and water from the destruction of petroleum infrastructure.

stories.title: Heritage sites in the Middle East under threat due to conflict
stories.summary: UNESCO reports at least six heritage sites in the Middle East have been damaged during the ongoing conflict, including the Tyre site in Lebanon, four sites in Iran—including Isfahan's historic city and Tehran's Golestan Palace—and Israel's White City in Tel Aviv.

stories.title: Iran 'dismisses' US 15-point peace plan, issues its own ceasefire proposal
stories.summary: Iran rejected a 15-point American peace plan on March 25 and issued its own counterproposal while continuing attacks on Israel and Gulf Arab states. Iran's conditions include a halt to targeted killings of its officials, security guarantees against future wars, war reparations, and recognition of Iranian sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Iran rejects US proposal to end war, calls it 'excessive,' official tells Iranian state TV
stories.summary: Iran rejected a US diplomatic proposal aimed at ending nearly four weeks of hostilities between the two countries, with an Iranian official describing the terms as 'excessive' on state television. Washington continues to push for a negotiated resolution to the conflict.

stories.title: Russia’s oil revenues hit four-year high amid Iran’s war. And Ukraine is paying price
stories.summary: Russia's oil revenues have reached a four-year high during the Iran conflict, with exports generating approximately $270 million per day. The revenue surge is compounding economic pressure on Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran, Nigeria, and Africa’s oil dependency
stories.summary: The war on Iran has raised questions about Africa's dependency on foreign energy supplies, particularly in Nigeria. Analysts are examining whether the conflict could push African nations toward greater energy independence.

stories.title: Trump accuses 'Radical Left' of undermining ‘military achievement’ in Iran
stories.summary: President Trump accused political opponents he called "Radical Left" Democrats of attempting to undermine US military operations in the war on Iran. In a Truth Social post, Trump claimed they were creating internal turmoil to distract from what he described as US successes.

stories.title: Starmer reaffirms UK support for ICC when asked about Karim Khan exoneration report
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer reaffirmed British support for the International Criminal Court when asked about a report clearing ICC prosecutor Karim Khan of wrongdoing. Starmer declined to comment on the court's internal proceedings.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones crash in Estonia and Latvia, raising air defence concerns
stories.summary: Stray Ukrainian drones crashed in Estonia and Latvia on March 25, with one striking a chimney at a power station. No injuries were reported, and the drones were believed to be part of a Ukrainian strike on Russian energy infrastructure. Latvian officials warned that such incursions could recur across the Baltic region.

stories.title: Iran’s regime was teetering. This war could be keeping it from collapse
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran may be inadvertently strengthening the Iranian regime rather than hastening its collapse. Experts argue the strikes have hardened the resolve of figures whose defection would be essential to bringing down the Islamic Republic.

stories.title: Army’s digital marketplace for drones is officially open
stories.summary: The U.S. Army officially launched a digital marketplace for drone procurement at an event in Huntsville, Alabama. Col. Danielle Medaglia, head of the Army's UAS project management office, said the platform accelerates acquisition by allowing manufacturers to offer systems when ready, replacing lengthy traditional competition processes.

stories.title: Spanish PM Sanchez attacks Netanyahu: 'He wants to do to Lebanon what he did to Gaza'
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez criticized Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, warning that Israel's military actions in Lebanon mirror those previously carried out in Gaza. Sanchez also cautioned about the broader economic consequences of the ongoing war involving Iran.

stories.title: As Israel prepares to intensify ground offensive in Lebanon, what can be learned from past wars?
stories.summary: As Israel prepares to expand its ground offensive in Lebanon, analysts are drawing comparisons to its 1967 doctrine of holding conquered territory after the Six-Day War. Whether this post-October 7 approach will prove effective in Lebanon remains uncertain.

stories.title: Iran rejects US plan to pause war, but what are their demands?
stories.summary: Iran formally rejected the US 15-point ceasefire proposal while putting forward its own set of demands. The two sides' contrasting conditions highlight significant gaps in negotiations to halt the conflict.

stories.title: Russian attacks knock out power for thousands in Ukraine's north
stories.summary: Russian attacks damaged two energy facilities in Ukraine's northern Chernihiv region, leaving approximately 212,000 consumers without power, according to a regional electricity distribution company on Wednesday.

stories.title: US has caused $10tn worth of climate damage since 1990, research finds
stories.summary: New research found that the United States has caused approximately $10 trillion in global economic damage since 1990 through its planet-heating carbon emissions. As the largest cumulative carbon emitter in history, the U.S. surpasses China, which is responsible for an estimated $9 trillion in GDP damage over the same period.

stories.title: War on Iran: What troops is the US moving to the Gulf?
stories.summary: The US military is increasing its troop deployments and assets in the Persian Gulf region around Iran. The growing buildup suggests a possible shift from an air campaign to potential ground operations.

stories.title: Video: Spanish PM says 'nightmare of Iraq will repeat itself'
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez warned that the US-Israeli war on Iran would replicate the consequences of the Iraq war. Sanchez made the remarks in a video statement shared on social media.

stories.title: Ukraine is asking world to sign  appeal to expel Russia from UNESCO after 17th-century Lviv monastery attack
stories.summary: Ukraine's Institute of National Memory launched an open appeal urging UNESCO and international partners to expel Russia from the organization. The call follows a Russian attack on a 17th-century monastery in Lviv.

stories.title: Ukraine attacks sparked fire at major Russian port, says governor
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes sparked a fire at a major Russian port, according to a regional governor. Russia had previously launched nearly 1,000 drones at Ukraine within a 24-hour period on March 24.

stories.title: Drone strike on Kharkiv: number of casualties has risen to nine
stories.summary: Russian strikes on the city of Kharkiv on the afternoon of March 25 injured at least nine people. The attack involved drone strikes on the Ukrainian city.

stories.title: War could cause 'worst industrial crisis in living memory'
stories.summary: The head of the International Chamber of Commerce, John Denton, warned that the Middle East war could trigger the worst industrial crisis in living memory. The International Energy Agency has characterized the situation as an energy crisis more severe than the 1970s oil shocks.

stories.title: Iran gives negative response to US ceasefire plan amid push for talks
stories.summary: Iranian officials gave an initial negative response to a 15-point U.S. ceasefire plan delivered by Pakistani intermediaries. The proposal included sanctions relief, dismantling Iran's nuclear program, missile restrictions, and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Intermediaries suggested direct U.S.-Iran talks could begin as early as the coming weekend.

stories.title: UN calls on Libyan authorities to release political activist
stories.summary: The UN Support Mission in Libya called on Libyan authorities to release political activist Al-Mahdi Abdulati. The UN mission warned of ongoing arbitrary detentions and broader human rights concerns in the country.

stories.title: Mobile app-based fuel quota system finalised for motorcycles, rickshaws amid global oil crisis
stories.summary: Pakistan's government has finalized a mobile application-based fuel quota system for motorcycles and rickshaws, and possibly vehicles up to 800cc. The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority and relevant ministries developed and tested the system to target fuel subsidies toward low-income users and reduce overall oil consumption.

stories.title: 'Ethnic cleansing': Israel evicts 11 Palestinian families from Jerusalem neighbourhood
stories.summary: Israel evicted 11 Palestinian families from a neighborhood in occupied East Jerusalem. Video footage showed settlers discarding furniture from Palestinian homes in the Silwan area, drawing accusations of ethnic cleansing from critics.

stories.title: What the Iran War reveals about missile warfare - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Analyst Tal Inbar examined the challenges of intercepting cluster munitions and assessed the performance of Israel's air defense systems during the Iran war. The analysis explores implications for Israel's future military strategy.

stories.title: Hezbollah fired 120 rockets from Tyre's neighborhoods, using civilians as shields, IDF says
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces stated that Hezbollah launched approximately 120 rockets from residential neighborhoods in Tyre, southern Lebanon. IDF spokesperson Avichay Adraee accused Hezbollah of using civilians as shields while operating on behalf of Iran's agenda.

stories.title: No, China Doesn’t Want Spheres of Influence
stories.summary: An analysis argues that characterizing China's ambitions as seeking spheres of influence both overstates and understates Beijing's actual strategic goals.

stories.title: Block on political crypto donations and a £100k cap from Britons abroad to take effect today – UK politics live
stories.summary: The UK has enacted new rules blocking political donations made via cryptocurrency and imposing a £100,000 cap on donations from British citizens living abroad. The measures follow the Rycroft review into political funding, with Health Secretary Steve Reed making a statement to MPs on the changes.

stories.title: NATO and Ukraine just launched their first joint defense tech competition. €10 million is the prize
stories.summary: NATO and Ukraine jointly launched their first defense technology competition under the UNITE — Brave NATO program, offering a €10 million prize. The initiative brings together companies from Ukraine and NATO member states to develop innovative defense solutions.

stories.title: The Battle to End Palestinian Self-Determination
stories.summary: An analysis highlights that Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank face acute vulnerability as international attention remains focused on the Iran war, raising concerns about efforts to undermine Palestinian self-determination.

stories.title: Iran gives five conditions for ending war, official tells state TV
stories.summary: An unnamed Iranian official told state TV that Tehran has rejected the US ceasefire proposal and outlined five conditions for ending the war. The conditions include an end to assassinations, security guarantees, and defined reparations. The official stated Iran would end the war on its own terms.

stories.title: Russian forces shell Kherson and Bilozerka, injuring civilians
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the city of Kherson and the nearby village of Bilozerka in southern Ukraine, injuring four civilians in the morning attack.

stories.title: UN rights council demands 'reparation' for Iran strikes on Gulf
stories.summary: The UN Human Rights Council demanded that Iran halt strikes on Gulf states and pay reparations for damage caused. Gulf nations warned that Iranian attacks on civilians and energy infrastructure are threatening regional stability.

stories.title: MQM-P calls for revisiting proposed 28th Amendment, transforming ‘feudal democracy into participatory democracy’
stories.summary: The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) has called for a review of Pakistan's proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment. Chairman Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, speaking at a press conference in Karachi alongside party leaders Mustafa Kamal and Farooq Sattar, urged amendments to safeguard citizens' rights and strengthen democracy.

stories.title: Assad fall sees Syria freedom index boost but challenges remain
stories.summary: Syria's freedom index has improved following the fall of Bashar al-Assad's regime, which was among the world's most repressive. However, the country still faces significant challenges in consolidating political rights gains from the 2024 revolution.

stories.title: Pakistan’s cities to account for most heat-related deaths by 2050
stories.summary: A study by the Climate Impact Lab at the University of Chicago projects that Pakistan will see a net increase of 51 deaths per 100,000 people by 2050 due to rising temperatures. Urban areas are expected to account for most heat-related mortality, with low- and middle-income countries bearing 90 percent of premature climate-related deaths.

stories.title: Denmark braces for lengthy and challenging coalition talks
stories.summary: Denmark faces prolonged coalition negotiations after neither Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's left-wing bloc nor the right-wing parties secured a majority in Tuesday's general election. Frederiksen submitted her government's resignation to the king on March 25. Her Social Democrat party recorded its worst general election result since 1903.

stories.title: How countries are tackling the global energy crisis
stories.summary: With energy prices surging and the Strait of Hormuz remaining closed, countries worldwide are implementing measures to reduce energy demand. Strategies include four-day workweeks, petrol rationing, and lowering air conditioning usage.

stories.title: Once seeking de-escalation, Saudi Arabia now sees ‘no coexistence’ with hardline Iran
stories.summary: Analysts observe that Saudi Arabia has shifted from pursuing de-escalation with Iran to concluding that coexistence with a hardline Iranian regime is no longer viable. Persistent attacks on critical infrastructure, according to experts, have driven this harder-edged strategic reassessment across Gulf states.

stories.title: With war keeping customers and workers away, retailers struggle to keep doors open
stories.summary: Israeli retailers are struggling to stay open as the ongoing war keeps customers and workers away. Many small business owners have reduced hours or shut down entirely, with schools remaining closed and missile threats continuing.

stories.title: US goals shift: 'At the beginning of the Iran war, the US and Israel were on the same page'
stories.summary: Analysts at the Royal United Services Institute note that while the U.S. and Israel were initially aligned at the start of the Iran war, divergence has since emerged. The shift involves differences in coherence, messaging, and political intent rather than ultimate objectives, alongside Israel's expanding military operations in Lebanon.

stories.title: Food security concerns mount as Iran war hurts fertilizer trade
stories.summary: The ongoing Iran conflict is disrupting fertilizer trade through the Strait of Hormuz, raising food security concerns for import-dependent countries including Sudan, Somalia, Tanzania, and Mozambique. Fertilizer use in these regions is already among the lowest in the world.

stories.title: Edmond de Rothschild Paris offices raided in Epstein-linked probe into diplomat
stories.summary: French investigators raided the Paris offices of Swiss bank Edmond de Rothschild as part of a corruption probe linked to Jeffrey Epstein. The inquiry centers on French diplomat Fabrice Aidan, who was seconded to the United Nations from 2006 to 2013 and whose name appeared in over 200 U.S. Justice Department documents.

stories.title: Could the continent’s far right be suffering from a Trumplash?
stories.summary: France's National Rally party missed key targets in recent local elections, raising questions about whether European far-right movements are experiencing a backlash linked to Donald Trump. Setbacks for right-wing figures have also been noted in Italy, Slovenia, and Hungary, while mainstream parties have shown resilience.

stories.title: Hong Kong holds onto Art Basel crown for 5 more years thanks to new deal
stories.summary: Hong Kong secured a five-year extension as the exclusive regional host of Art Basel, the city's culture minister announced. Some galleries at a preview noted that global uncertainties had prompted collectors to increase interest in works from established artists.

stories.title: Exotic pet trade thrives in China despite welfare concerns
stories.summary: China's exotic pet industry is experiencing rapid growth, with a market approaching 10 billion yuan and approximately 17 million exotic pet owners nationwide. At a Beijing animal fair, animals such as meerkats and raccoons were sold and displayed, raising welfare concerns about cramped enclosures and the commodification of wild species.

stories.title: Iran war threatens to delay large offshore wind projects in EU and UK
stories.summary: Major offshore wind projects in the UK and EU face potential delays as the Iran war threatens shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz. Industry sources fear that crucial components manufactured in the United Arab Emirates could become stranded, affecting planned North Sea installations for the UK and Germany.

stories.title: Lars Løkke Rasmussen: Denmark’s pipe-smoking kingmaker who cleans his teeth with soap
stories.summary: Lars Løkke Rasmussen, leader of Denmark's centrist Moderates party and a two-time former prime minister, emerged as a kingmaker after Tuesday's general election. He is expected to play a central role in upcoming coalition negotiations. Rasmussen is also credited with easing tensions between Denmark and the U.S. over Greenland.

stories.title: Volkswagen in talks to make Iron Dome parts for Israel
stories.summary: German automaker Volkswagen is in talks to manufacture components for Israel's Iron Dome missile defense system. The potential move would mark a return to military-related manufacturing for the company, which has a controversial wartime history.

stories.title: Pack a Seder: How one box is reaching Israel's most isolated survivors
stories.summary: An initiative called Pack a Seder is delivering Passover supplies to isolated Holocaust survivors in Israel. Organizer Zalman Duchman said the program serves elderly survivors the organization supports throughout the year.

stories.title: Iran calls US proposal to end war ‘maximalist, unreasonable’
stories.summary: Iran has publicly rejected a US proposal to end the ongoing war, describing the terms as "maximalist" and "unreasonable." Details of the proposal and Iran's specific objections have not yet been fully disclosed.

stories.title: Nigeria: Three Killed, Many Injured As Violence Erupts in Nasarawa Community
stories.summary: Three people were killed and many injured in Nasarawa State, Nigeria, after violence erupted in the Aso A area of a community on Wednesday morning, reportedly sparked by a dispute between a mobile police officer and a herder.

stories.title: Dagenham leaseholders left homeless by fire could be forced to pay for cladding works
stories.summary: Former leaseholders of the Spectrum Building in Dagenham, east London, say they face bills for fire safety works on the tower block that was demolished after a major fire in August 2024. The Greater London Authority is seeking to reclaim £6 million allocated for uncompleted cladding remediation on the destroyed building.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria Unveils HIV Prevention Plan, Shifts Focus Beyond Treatment
stories.summary: Nigeria launched a new HIV prevention plan shifting its focus beyond treatment to address evolving infection patterns. The initiative aims to close gaps in the country's overall HIV response.

stories.title: Nigeria: Gov Speaks As Terrorists Gun Down Soldiers in Kebbi
stories.summary: Governor Nasir Idris of Kebbi State, Nigeria, expressed shock after terrorists killed several soldiers in the state. The attack highlights ongoing security challenges in northwestern Nigeria.

stories.title: Rwanda: Kagame Backs Revival of Muslims' Morning Call to Prayer
stories.summary: Rwandan President Paul Kagame reassured Muslims that the morning call to prayer will be restored. The practice had been disrupted as local government institutions implemented noise pollution regulations in Kigali and other areas.

stories.title: Iran’s Peace Negotiator Is His Country’s Trump
stories.summary: Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Ghalibaf has emerged as a key peace negotiator for Iran. His political rise has been characterized by populist imagery, allegations of real estate corruption, and a reputation for ruthlessness.

stories.title: War will end 'when Iran decides it', Iranian official tells state TV
stories.summary: Iranian state television reported that a senior official rejected the US-proposed ceasefire plan to end the war. The official stated that the conflict will end when Iran decides, not according to President Trump's timeline.

stories.title: Canada Faces Its Finland Moment
stories.summary: An analysis compares Canada's current geopolitical position to Finland's situation during the Cold War, arguing that Ottawa faces threats from a powerful and confrontational neighbor in the United States.

stories.title: Seeking a deal with different faces of the same regime, Trump risks subverting his own vital war goals
stories.summary: President Trump promised Iranians that after the war their government would be theirs to reclaim, but analysts question whether negotiations with the existing regime can achieve that goal. Critics warn his approach may undermine stated US war objectives, including guaranteed security for Israel.

stories.title: US demands of 15-point peace plan likely 'unacceptable' for Iran
stories.summary: The United States has sent a 15-point peace plan to Iran, which Tehran has publicly dismissed as excessive. Reported demands include sanctions relief, rollback of Iran's nuclear programme, IAEA monitoring, freedom of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, and an end to Iranian support for proxy groups.

stories.title: UN migration agency says 2025 was deadliest year on Red Sea migrant route
stories.summary: The International Organization for Migration reported that 2025 has been the deadliest year on record for the Red Sea migrant route. The number of people who died or went missing on the route doubled to 922.

stories.title: Airbus wins Chinese airline’s 101-plane order in victory over Boeing in key market
stories.summary: China Eastern Airlines placed a multibillion-dollar order for 101 Airbus A320neo aircraft, marking another win for the French manufacturer over rival Boeing in the Chinese market. While the list price would be approximately $15.8 billion, China Eastern said Airbus granted a significant discount.

stories.title: Should China be worried about Japan’s maritime force overhaul?
stories.summary: Japan's Maritime Self-Defence Force restructured its organizational framework on Monday to accelerate decision-making and improve ship operations, including preparations for quasi-carrier capabilities. Chinese analysts view the overhaul as reflecting Japan's shift toward preparations for a potential conflict with Beijing.

stories.title: Fifty years on, Israel repeats previous mistakes leading to the October 7 massacre - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel has repeated the intelligence failures that preceded the 1973 Yom Kippur War, contributing to the October 7, 2023 attack. The analysis highlights persistent blind spots over five decades and calls for urgent intelligence reform.

stories.title: Ukraine needs about two thousand anti-ballistic missiles per year – Kubilius
stories.summary: EU Defense Commissioner Andrius Kubilius stated that Ukraine requires approximately 2,000 anti-ballistic missiles per year. He noted that improvements in Russian ballistic missile capabilities have reduced interception effectiveness, increasing Ukraine's need for interceptors.

stories.title: In Nairobi, residents blame flood devastation on inadequate infrastructure
stories.summary: Flooding across at least 21 Kenyan counties since March has displaced over 34,000 people, with the capital Nairobi particularly hard hit. Residents blame the severity of the devastation on inadequate infrastructure and rapid urban growth. Nairobi's governor has launched emergency operations to clear drainage systems.

stories.title: Ghana and EU sign defence partnership to counter west Africa insecurity
stories.summary: Ghana and the European Union signed their first formal defence partnership on March 25 in Accra. Ghana also signed similar agreements with Iceland and Australia. The partnerships aim to counter growing insecurity in West Africa from groups linked to al-Qaeda and the Islamic State.

stories.title: Iran appears to target Israeli power plant in missile attack, but misses
stories.summary: Iran apparently targeted an Israeli power plant with a missile attack but missed. Separately, a senior Iranian official confirmed receiving the US peace proposal, and the Israeli Air Force struck Iran's sole submarine development facility.

stories.title: Saudi Pro League, the US or Europe - what are Salah's options?
stories.summary: Liverpool forward Mohamed Salah announced he will leave the club this summer. Analysts are examining his potential destinations, including the Saudi Pro League, the United States, or other European clubs.

stories.title: US defense giant taps Israeli drone navigation tech built for jammed battlefields
stories.summary: A US defense company has partnered with Israeli firm ASIO to use its drone navigation technology. The system is designed to keep unmanned aircraft operational in combat environments where GPS signals are jammed or denied.

stories.title: Pro-Iran Iraqi militias expand attacks into Syria
stories.summary: Pro-Iran Iraqi militias expanded their attacks into Syria, targeting the Kharab al-Jir base in Hasakah province on 23 March. Damascus says US forces had already withdrawn from the base in February 2026.

stories.title: GOP moving forward with new reconciliation bill, with money for defense: Graham
stories.summary: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Lindsey Graham announced that Republicans are advancing a second reconciliation bill that includes increased defense funding. Graham said the bill aims to ensure adequate resources for homeland security and to support U.S. military personnel engaged in combat operations.

stories.title: Missiles overhead, silence below: Israel’s home front holds firm
stories.summary: Israel's home front is holding together amid ongoing Iranian missile attacks, with a combination of military censorship and public unity suppressing dissent. The prolonged conflict with Iran has tested civilian resilience across the country.

stories.title: Anthropic’s case against the Pentagon could open space for AI regulation
stories.summary: A California judge has suggested the US Department of Defense may be attempting to undermine Anthropic, the AI company, for advocating restrictions on AI weapons systems. The case could set precedents for AI regulation in the defense sector.

stories.title: Iran struggles to assert control in Iraq amid strikes, militia attacks, tensions - analysis
stories.summary: Iran is struggling to maintain influence in Iraq following strikes and militia activity. Kurdish leaders in the autonomous region have expressed outrage over an Iranian attack, prompting Tehran to appear to walk back the incident, though it continues asserting control elsewhere in the country.

stories.title: Fedorov holds discussions with representatives of 13 assault and infantry units
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov held a closed meeting with representatives of 13 assault and infantry units to discuss front-line conditions. Topics included service term policies and financial support for soldiers.

stories.title: Russia pulls more staff from Iran nuclear plant after reported strike
stories.summary: Russia evacuated an additional 163 staff from Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant following a reported overnight strike on the compound. Rosatom CEO Alexey Likhachev said approximately 300 Russian personnel remain at the facility, which Russia partially constructed.

stories.title: Ukraine: Massive wave of daytime Russian strikes hits sites nationwide
stories.summary: Russia launched nearly 1,000 drones at targets across Ukraine on March 24 in one of the largest daytime air strikes since the war began. The attacks killed several people and caused damage in multiple cities, some located hundreds of kilometres from the front lines.

stories.title: Danish election signals shift toward Dutch and Belgian-style of coalition building
stories.summary: Following Denmark's general election, analysts observe a shift toward fragmented, negotiation-heavy coalition politics resembling models seen in the Netherlands and Belgium. Traditional parties experienced electoral erosion, though not uniformly. External crises influenced public perception but did not singularly determine voting outcomes.

stories.title: Musketeer d'Artagnan's remains believed found under Dutch church
stories.summary: Archaeologists believe they have discovered the remains of Charles de Batz-Castelmore d'Artagnan, the historical figure who inspired Alexandre Dumas's famous musketeer character, beneath a church in the Netherlands. D'Artagnan was killed during the 1673 Siege of Maastricht.

stories.title: State Duma Members to Travel to U.S. in Coming Days for Congressional Talks
stories.summary: A delegation of four or five Russian State Duma members is expected to travel to Washington, D.C. in the coming days for talks with members of the U.S. Congress.

stories.title: Hezbollah chief urges unity, no talks with Israel amid Lebanon attacks
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem called for unity against Israel and rejected any negotiations while Lebanon is under attack. He stated that negotiating under fire would amount to imposing surrender on Lebanon.

stories.title: Ukrainian grain was stolen, relabeled Russian, and sold to a UN food program supplier—the paperwork said nothing about Mariupol
stories.summary: An investigation found that grain stolen from Ukrainian territories, including Mariupol, was relabeled as Russian and sold to a UN World Food Programme supplier in Turkey. The same Russian family involved reportedly also manufactures attack drones for Russia's military.

stories.title: Russian drone makers sell stolen Ukrainian grain—part reaching a UN food supplier
stories.summary: An investigation found that a Russian family involved in manufacturing attack drones for Russia's war in Ukraine also exports stolen Ukrainian grain. Some of the wheat reportedly reached a supplier for a UN food program operating in Turkey.

stories.title: Israeli court closes case into Palestinian teen’s death despite evidence of starvation
stories.summary: An Israeli court closed an investigation into the death of 17-year-old Palestinian Walid Ahmad, who died in Israeli custody in March 2025 amid evidence of starvation. Human rights experts condemned the ruling, citing ongoing impunity as prisoner deaths continue to mount.

stories.title: Israeli attacks hit Gaza shelters and aid site despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit shelters and an aid distribution site in Gaza despite a ceasefire being in place, killing and wounding Palestinians. UN officials warned of deepening humanitarian crisis and ceasefire violations.

stories.title: Are Middle East attacks pushing Asia towards an energy crisis?
stories.summary: Attacks on energy facilities across the Middle East, including Qatar's LNG infrastructure, are driving global energy prices higher. Asian economies that depend heavily on Middle Eastern energy imports face growing concerns about a potential energy crisis.

stories.title: Latvia and Estonia confirm crash of Ukrainian drones
stories.summary: Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics confirmed that a Ukrainian drone crashed in Latvia's Kraslava region on March 25 while en route to strike targets in Russia. Estonia also confirmed a similar incident on its territory the same night.

stories.title: Semicon China: AI, advanced packaging set to drive country’s chip industry growth
stories.summary: China's chip industry is expected to account for approximately 42 percent of global wafer fabrication capacity by 2028, according to data presented at Semicon China. Agentic artificial intelligence and advanced packaging technology were identified as key growth drivers for the sector.

stories.title: Pentagon, Lockheed sign plan to boost PrSM missile production
stories.summary: The Pentagon and Lockheed Martin have signed a plan to boost production of the Precision Strike Missile (PrSM). BAE Systems and Honeywell Aerospace have also signed new framework agreements to increase munitions production over the coming years.

stories.title: Russia building satellite network to replace Starlink, launches first 16 into orbit
stories.summary: Russia launched the first 16 satellites for a new network called Rassvet, meaning 'Dawn,' intended as a domestic alternative to SpaceX's Starlink constellation. The project aims to provide independent satellite communication capability.

stories.title: Lebanese court issues arrest warrants against Hezbollah terrorists for weapons smuggling
stories.summary: A Lebanese court issued arrest warrants for Hezbollah operatives accused of smuggling weapons into southern Lebanon. Two suspects reportedly admitted to transporting arms intended for attacks against Israeli military forces, claiming such actions were justified under international law.

stories.title: 14-year-old boy indicted for spying for Iran in exchange for money
stories.summary: Israeli prosecutors indicted a 14-year-old boy for allegedly spying for Iran in exchange for payment. The minor reportedly contacted an Iranian agent via Telegram and filmed footage of a hospital and residential areas, and was asked to surveil Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar.

stories.title: UN confirms Gaza security force to include Kazakhstan, Indonesia and Morocco
stories.summary: The United Nations confirmed that Kazakhstan, Indonesia, and Morocco will participate in a security force for Gaza. Discussions over the composition of the stabilization force have been ongoing since September 2025.

stories.title: Australians can expect high fuel costs to linger for far longer than the war in Iran
stories.summary: Diesel prices in Australia have surpassed $3 per litre in nearly every capital city amid disruptions linked to the Iran war. Trucking operators and farmers warn they may go out of business, with potential knock-on effects for food prices. Economists caution the inflationary impact could outlast the conflict itself.

stories.title: Long-promised animal cruelty prevention laws quietly shelved by Victorian government
stories.summary: The Victorian state government in Australia has quietly shelved long-promised animal cruelty prevention legislation that would have recognized all animals as sentient. The Labor bill, which aimed to raise care requirements, will not be introduced before the next state election despite being pledged nearly a decade ago.

stories.title: China still on track to supplant US as world’s No 1 economy in 10 years: academic
stories.summary: A University of Hong Kong academic said China remains on track to surpass the United States as the world's largest economy within the next decade. Li Cheng argued that while China faces a structural economic transition, current U.S. challenges—including what he called self-defeating policies—are more severe.

stories.title: Small petrol stations urge Albanese government to crack down on fuel wholesalers as operators run dry
stories.summary: Independent petrol station operators and miners in Australia are urging the Albanese government to crack down on major fuel wholesalers accused of hoarding supply. Smaller operators, particularly in rural and regional areas, report running out of fuel amid disruptions caused by the Iran war.

stories.title: Israel using white phosphorus to scorch earth in south Lebanon, researcher says
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch says it has verified and geolocated images showing Israel using white phosphorus munitions over southern Lebanon. Researchers identified the weapon by its distinctive airburst plume from M825-series artillery projectiles. The use of white phosphorus in civilian areas has drawn accusations of violations of the laws of war.

stories.title: ‘Makes Covid look like a tea party’: Australian food prices could rise for the next year, farmers warn
stories.summary: Australian farmers warn that food prices could rise for at least the next year due to the Iran conflict's impact on fuel, fertiliser, and petrochemical supply chains. Norco dairy cooperative CEO Michael Hampson said a six-to-twelve-month disruption is a best-case scenario, contingent on the Strait of Hormuz reopening.

stories.title: Philippines says it is working with US to obtain oil from US-sanctioned nations
stories.summary: The Philippines declared a national energy emergency on Tuesday due to oil supply disruptions from the Middle East war. Its ambassador to the U.S. said Manila is working with Washington to obtain waivers allowing it to purchase oil from U.S.-sanctioned countries.

stories.title: Suspicious bets placed on US-Iran strikes trigger insider trading concerns
stories.summary: Suspicious trading activity involving thousands of oil contracts occurred approximately 15 minutes before U.S. President Trump announced on March 25 that he would step back from threatening Iranian energy sites. The trades, which would have profited from falling crude prices, have raised concerns about potential insider trading.

stories.title: US and Czech citizens placed in pretrial detention over arson at plant supplying Ukraine — Czech intelligence asks if Russia used pro-Palestinian group as cover
stories.summary: Czech authorities placed US and Czech citizens in pretrial detention over an arson attack on a plant supplying materials to Ukraine. Czech intelligence is investigating whether Russia used a pro-Palestinian group as cover for the operation; one suspect shouted 'Free Palestine' upon arrest.

stories.title: General Staff confirms strike on Novatek-Ust-Luga plant in Russia's Leningrad region
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a strike on the Novatek-Ust-Luga plant in Russia's Leningrad region, verifying earlier reports of the attack on the energy facility.

stories.title: UK to host talks on mission to reopen Hormuz, says official
stories.summary: Britain and France will chair military talks involving approximately 30 nations to form a coalition aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The UK-hosted discussions follow a joint statement by six countries expressing readiness to ensure safe passage through the strait, subsequently endorsed by 24 additional nations.

stories.title: Lebanon state media says Israeli strikes kill 9 in south
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed nine people in southern Lebanon, according to Lebanese state media. Hezbollah said its fighters launched multiple attacks targeting Israeli troops in south Lebanon and inside Israel.

stories.title: Israel talks up Iranian threats to European cities to justify war
stories.summary: Israel has been framing Iran as a threat to European cities in an effort to build international support for its war against Tehran. The campaign aims to persuade European governments that the conflict serves broader Western security interests.

stories.title: Nigeria moves to broaden security alliances amid ongoing insurgency threats
