stories.summary: The Australian government is preparing for global oil prices to exceed US$120 per barrel as diesel prices surpass A$3 per litre nationwide. Energy Minister noted fuel stocks are at the same level as when the US and Israel launched military operations against Iran a month ago. Expanded ethanol mandates are among options under consideration.

stories.title: Pakistan joins UNSC in denouncing illegal Israeli settlements
stories.summary: Pakistan joined seven other UN Security Council members in condemning Israel's annexation of occupied Palestinian territory and the forcible displacement of Palestinians, stating such actions violate international law and undermine peace prospects.

stories.title: ‘Massive betrayal’: Iranian nationals with valid tourist visas blocked from entering Australia for six months
stories.summary: Australia's Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke imposed a six-month ban on Iranian nationals with valid tourist visas entering Australia, citing concerns they may be unable to return to Iran. The ban could affect more than 7,000 visa holders, though some may receive special consideration.

stories.title: Trump's stringent demands on Iran risk bogging down potential talks, sources say
stories.summary: The United States has issued sweeping demands to Iran as a condition for ending the war, which sources say Tehran is likely to reject. Turkey, Pakistan, and Egypt have been attempting to establish a diplomatic channel between Washington and Tehran to facilitate ceasefire talks.

stories.title: US mulls sending elite airborne troops to Middle East
stories.summary: The United States is considering deploying approximately 3,000 soldiers from the 82nd Airborne Division to the Middle East to support operations against Iran. Meanwhile, Israel claimed a large wave of strikes on Isfahan and other Iranian areas, and Iran reported a projectile hit its Bushehr nuclear power plant.

stories.title: BBC and NWA: the day ABC staff went on strike – and left Aunty looking ‘a bit different’
stories.summary: More than 2,000 ABC staff in Australia walked off the job on Wednesday in their first strike in two decades, protesting working conditions. The public broadcaster's news channel switched to BBC programming, while other networks filled airtime with reruns and alternative content.

stories.title: Five Wargames Every Force Design Process Needs
stories.summary: A 2019 Marine Corps planning initiative under Commandant Gen. David Berger identified wargaming as critical to force design modernization. Over 20 major wargames were conducted in the first two years of Force Design 2030, drawing lessons from interwar-period military planning exercises.

stories.title: Islamabad offers to host US-Iran climbdown effort
stories.summary: Pakistan formally offered to host U.S.-Iran negotiations in Islamabad, with U.S. envoy Witkoff expected to lead the American engagement. Qatar and Turkey also expressed support for swift efforts to end the conflict, while Tehran acknowledged receiving and responding to U.S. messages through a backchannel.

stories.title: Ukraine’s UNESCO envoy: Russia’s membership unacceptable over cultural heritage crimes
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ambassador to France and UNESCO representative Vadym Omelchenko called on UNESCO's Director-General to assess Russia's attacks on cultural heritage sites. He argued that Russia's continued membership in the organization is unacceptable given these actions.

stories.title: More than 5,000 Israelis injured since start of war, health ministry says
stories.summary: Israel's health ministry reported that over 5,000 people have been hospitalized since the war with Iran began on February 28. In the past 24 hours alone, 204 injured individuals were admitted, with 120 patients currently remaining in hospitals.

stories.title: International convoy delivers tons of aid to Cuba amid crisis
stories.summary: Cuba received a humanitarian aid shipment on Tuesday from the Nuestra America Convoy, an international initiative organized by global activists. The effort aims to circumvent U.S. sanctions that severely restrict fuel and other goods from reaching the island.

stories.title: Senior Japanese minister expresses regret over military officer’s arrest at Chinese embassy
stories.summary: A Japanese Ground Self-Defence Force second lieutenant, Kodai Murata, 23, was arrested on suspicion of trespassing at the Chinese embassy in Tokyo while carrying an 18-centimeter knife. No one was injured, and the blade was found in shrubbery on the embassy grounds. A senior Japanese official and the military expressed regret over the incident.

stories.title: Iran’s new security boss Mohammad Zolghadr: Why his appointment matters
stories.summary: Iran appointed Mohammad Zolghadr, a former IRGC commander, as its new security chief. He is tasked with managing internal unrest and external pressures from the United States and Israel.

stories.title: Proxy Pressure on Iran: The Promise and Pitfalls of Arming the Kurds
stories.summary: Early in the US-Iran war, the Trump administration and Israel attempted to foment an uprising in Iran by arming Kurdish fighters along the Iran-Iraq border. While Kurdish groups had proven capable as US battlefield partners against the Islamic State in Syria, the strategy of using them inside Iran carried significant risks.

stories.title: US said to have sent Iran a plan to end the Middle East war
stories.summary: The U.S. reportedly sent Iran a plan to end the Middle East war, though it remains unclear whether Israel has endorsed the proposal. The development comes amid ongoing hostilities in the region.

stories.title: 'The humanitarian crisis here is worsening by the minute': Israel continues to bomb Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's continued bombardment of Lebanon has displaced more than one million people, with the humanitarian crisis deepening. Israeli forces have also seized territory south of the Litani River, fueling resentment among the Lebanese population.

stories.title: Nazi-era weapons maker Volkswagen eyes return to arms production, this time with Israel
stories.summary: German automaker Volkswagen is exploring plans to enter arms production through defense ties with Israel. The move comes as the company faces competitive pressure from China in the automotive industry.

stories.title: Cyprus seeks new security deal for UK bases, Telegraph reports
stories.summary: Cyprus has requested that the United Kingdom negotiate new security arrangements for British military bases on the island, following Iranian drone attacks earlier in March, according to a report by The Telegraph.

stories.title: Zelensky discusses SAFE program and joint drone production with Latvian defense minister
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Latvian Defense Minister Andris Spruds to discuss strengthening air defense and joint drone production. The leaders also explored expanding cooperation within the SAFE framework.

stories.title: UK inflation held at 3% before global energy price hit from Iran war
stories.summary: UK inflation held steady at 3% in February, matching analysts' expectations, though the rate remains above the government's 2% target. The outlook has since shifted due to rising global energy costs driven by the war between the US-Israel coalition and Iran.

stories.title: Israeli forces turn Palestinian homes into military bases
stories.summary: Israeli forces have been taking over Palestinian homes in two communities in the occupied West Bank, converting them into military bases. Residents near Hebron reported that soldiers occupied their homes for days at a time.

stories.title: Is Amazon Ads silencing Palestinian books?
stories.summary: Independent Palestinian publishers have raised concerns that Amazon Ads may be blocking or limiting the visibility of titles related to Palestine. The allegations point to potential suppression of Palestinian literature on the platform.

stories.title: Follow the Money: Finance and the Future of Allied Economic Statecraft
stories.summary: An analysis examines how the global flow of capital across defense, infrastructure, manufacturing, and technology sectors is becoming central to great-power competition. Governments are increasingly aligning national security priorities with private investment through new economic statecraft tools.

stories.title: Saudi prince is said to push Trump to continue Iran war in recent calls
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has reportedly urged US President Donald Trump in recent phone calls to continue military operations against Iran, leveraging his previously demonstrated influence on Trump's foreign policy decisions.

stories.title: US-Israel war on Iran: What’s happening on day 26 of attacks?
stories.summary: On day 26 of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, new missile and drone exchanges occurred involving Iran, Israel, and Gulf states. The United States signaled both military escalation and openness to a negotiated deal.

stories.title: New Mexico jury says Meta harms children’s mental health and safety, violating state law
stories.summary: A New Mexico jury found Meta liable for harming children's mental health and safety, ruling the company violated state law. The verdict followed a nearly seven-week trial. A separate federal case in California involving Meta and YouTube is also under deliberation.

stories.title: Video: Trump claims talks led him to delay strike on Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated he had delayed a planned strike on Iran's largest electricity generation plant because negotiations were ongoing. Speaking at a swearing-in ceremony, Trump also claimed Iran had agreed to never pursue nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Iran says will 'absolutely' continue charging vessels for Hormuz passage
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei confirmed that Tehran will continue charging vessels fees for passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The restrictions on the key shipping route remain in place due to the ongoing war.

stories.title: How is the Philippines reacting to its energy emergency?
stories.summary: BBC News Asia Business Correspondent Suranjana Tewari reported from a petrol station in Manila on the Philippines' response to a declared energy emergency, as the country grapples with fuel supply challenges.

stories.title: Indian man whose life support was removed after court go-ahead dies
stories.summary: Harish Rana, a 31-year-old Indian man who had been in a comatose state since falling from a fourth-floor balcony in 2013, has died after a court authorized the removal of his life support.

stories.title: Malaysia’s weather is so hot that it can warp a payment card
stories.summary: Extreme heat across peninsular Malaysia, particularly in the northern states of Kedah and Perlis, is posing health risks and disrupting daily life. The scorching temperatures dampened Eid holiday celebrations, with families adjusting routines and farmers monitoring paddy fields under intense sun.

stories.title: Drone destroys private home in Odesa region, one injured, possible person trapped under rubble
stories.summary: In the Odesa region of Ukraine, an enemy drone struck and destroyed a private residential building, sparking a large fire. At least one person was injured, and another may be trapped under the rubble.

stories.title: Former Qatari prime minister urges GCC role in US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Former Qatari Prime Minister Hamad bin Jassim al-Thani called for Gulf Cooperation Council states to be included in any US-Iran negotiations. He stressed that the Strait of Hormuz should not be used as a bargaining chip and that the region's future cannot be decided without Gulf involvement.

stories.title: Where does Salah rank among greatest Premier League forwards?
stories.summary: Mohamed Salah confirmed his departure from Liverpool at the end of the season. BBC Sport invited fans to rank the best forwards in Premier League history in light of the announcement.

stories.title: South Korean ‘sugar cane killer’ extradited from Philippines over drug empire
stories.summary: South Korean national Park Wang-yeol, 48, known as the "sugar cane killer," was extradited from the Philippines to South Korea after nine years of failed attempts. Investigators allege he ran a drug trafficking empire from inside a Philippine prison, maintaining a VIP lifestyle.

stories.title: Iran says 243 students and teachers killed as nearly 500 schools targeted
stories.summary: Iran's Education Ministry reported that at least 243 students and teachers have been killed since the war began on February 28, with nearly 500 schools targeted. Iran's Red Crescent Society said more than 80,000 civilian structures have been damaged or destroyed in US and Israeli strikes.

stories.title: Morning recap
stories.summary: Tensions continued across the Middle East as Israeli and Iranian military strikes intensified. Washington reportedly sent Iran a proposal including nuclear rollback and ceasefire terms, while Iran's military spokesperson rejected US negotiation claims.

stories.title: Facing violence on all fronts, Arab Israelis are unprecedentedly open to mental health help
stories.summary: The Community Stress Prevention Center in northern Israel has observed increased openness to mental health services among Arab Israeli communities after 18 months of expanded outreach. The shift comes as Arab Israelis face violence on multiple fronts, with stigmas around seeking help beginning to break down.

stories.title: Leniency shown to Hong Kong immigration worker who repeatedly assaulted wife and son
stories.summary: A Hong Kong court placed a 49-year-old senior Immigration Department assistant on one-year probation after he was convicted of repeatedly choking his wife and young son during domestic disputes. The defendant requested probation over community service to avoid losing his job and pension.

stories.title: Football: France have arrived in Boston to face Brazil and Colombia
stories.summary: The French national football team arrived in Boston for a US tour, with matches scheduled against Brazil on March 26 and Colombia on March 29.

stories.title: Police chief who responded to Detroit synagogue attack targeted by online vitriol
stories.summary: A police chief involved in the response to a synagogue attack in Detroit has faced antisemitic harassment online. A man who posted an antisemitic meme of the non-Jewish sheriff was arrested on an unrelated charge, prompting far-right figures to claim censorship.

stories.title: Taiwan says US has 'high' urgency in speeding up weapons deliveries
stories.summary: Taiwan said there is "high" urgency for the United States to speed up weapons deliveries. Taiwan has complained of repeated delays to arms orders from the US, its most important international backer, amid a rising military threat from China.

stories.title: Recap of todays events
stories.summary: Iran notified the International Maritime Organisation it would allow non-hostile shipping through the Strait of Hormuz while excluding US- and Israel-linked vessels. US President Trump said the US was in contact with "the right people" in Iran regarding potential talks.

stories.title: Israel approves proposal to build permanent US embassy in Jerusalem
stories.summary: The Israeli government approved a proposal to construct a permanent U.S. embassy in Jerusalem. The decision was jointly announced by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Foreign Affairs Minister Gideon Sa'ar, and Construction and Housing Minister Haim Katz.

stories.title: Antisemitic attacks in Europe raise questions about new, shadowy ‘terror group’
stories.summary: A previously unknown group called Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya has been linked to a string of arson attacks targeting Jewish sites in Europe. Some analysts suggest the shadowy organization may have ties to pro-Iranian militias.

stories.title: China yam with human ‘fingernails’, 260 free meals, lottery win after lifetime of playing
stories.summary: A man in Jieyang, Guangdong province in southern China, unearthed a Chinese yam shaped remarkably like a human hand, appearing to have fingernails and skin. The unusual shape went viral online, though yams commonly grow into irregular forms due to soil conditions.

stories.title: Iran war live: Israel says it will control bridges and area south of Lebanon’s Litani River
stories.summary: Israel announced it would control bridges and territory south of Lebanon's Litani River. Meanwhile, Iran dismissed Trump's claims of ongoing negotiations as "fake news," and Shell's CEO warned fuel shortages could reach Europe within a month.

stories.title: UK's Starmer, Saudi crown prince discussed ongoing Middle East conflict, Downing Street says
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer spoke with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Tuesday evening about the ongoing Middle East conflict, according to a Downing Street spokesperson.

stories.title: Talk of annexation in Lebanon risks undermining Israel’s case against Hezbollah - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial warned that Israeli rhetoric about annexing territory up to Lebanon's Litani River risks undermining Israel's case against Hezbollah. While securing the northern border is considered justified, talk of annexation carries strategic and diplomatic costs.

stories.title: Airline boss flags possible fuel rationing in Philippines as supplies dwindle
stories.summary: Philippine Airlines president Richard Nuttall said the Philippines may need to implement fuel rationing due to tight supplies caused by the war in Iran. He made the remarks at the Aviation Festival Asia conference in Singapore, highlighting the impact of the conflict on regional fuel availability.

stories.title: Trump insists talks happening ‘right now’ as Iran, Israel trade strikes
stories.summary: President Trump claimed that negotiations related to the Iran conflict are currently underway, stating that Iran gave him a "very big present" related to oil and gas without providing further details. The remarks came as Iran and Israel continued exchanging military strikes.

stories.title: Ukraine war briefing: Moldova declares emergency after Russian attack cuts key power line
stories.summary: Moldova declared a 60-day state of emergency in its energy sector after Russian drone strikes in Ukraine severed a key power line connecting Moldova to Europe. Prime Minister Alexandru Munteanu urged citizens to reduce electricity consumption, especially during peak hours.

stories.title: Iranian military scoffs at US attempts at a ceasefire deal
stories.summary: An Iranian military spokesperson from the Khatam Al-Anbiya Central Headquarters mocked Washington's proposed 15-point ceasefire plan, casting doubt on its viability. The plan was submitted to Tehran by intermediaries amid President Trump's stated desire to end the conflict.

stories.title: Amid US-Israeli attacks, people in Iran struggle to survive ailing economy
stories.summary: Iranian civilians are facing severe economic hardship amid ongoing US and Israeli attacks. Many have lost their incomes, others have been temporarily displaced, and internet services remain disrupted across the country.

stories.title: Hong Kong, Hainan can ‘forge strong partnership’, build on strengths: John Lee
stories.summary: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee urged closer cooperation between Hong Kong and China's Hainan province, calling on businesses to leverage Hainan's free-trade port status. Lee made the remarks after meeting Hainan's Communist Party Secretary Feng Fei at the Boao Forum for Asia.

stories.title: Humanitarian aid boat arrives in Cuba amid US blockade crisis
stories.summary: A humanitarian aid boat named "Granma 2.0" carrying medical supplies, food, and solar panels arrived in Havana from Mexico as part of a flotilla effort. The delivery aimed to assist Cuba as a US fuel blockade deepens the island's energy crisis.

stories.title: Intelligence officers capture two more Russian soldiers in Zaporizhzhia sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Intelligence special forces captured two Russian soldiers during stabilization operations in the Zaporizhzhia sector of the front line.

stories.title: China’s consumer goods factories cut output as Iran war sends costs soaring
stories.summary: Some Chinese manufacturers are reducing production as the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz disrupts shipping and drives up energy, raw material, and freight costs. A bicycle factory owner in Guangzhou reported a 30% rise in aluminum costs and has suspended most export orders, including all orders from Iran.

stories.title: As Iran war rocks global economy, Global South bears brunt of fallout
stories.summary: Developing economies in Asia, Africa, and the Middle East are bearing the heaviest impact from the Iran war's economic fallout. Surging energy costs driven by the conflict are disproportionately affecting the Global South.

stories.title: Kenya: Men Accounted for 90% of Victims of Police Killings in Kenya in 2025 - Missing Voices Report
stories.summary: A report by Kenya's Missing Voices Coalition found that men accounted for approximately 90% of victims of police killings in Kenya in 2025. The findings highlight persistent gendered patterns in the use of force by Kenyan security agencies.

stories.title: Uganda: Police Vacate Bobi Wine's Magere Home After Two-Month Siege
stories.summary: Ugandan police fully withdrew from the private residence of opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi, known as Bobi Wine, in Magere, Wakiso District. The departure ended a two-month siege that had effectively restricted access to the property.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran launches strikes on US bases in Gulf; oil prices drop after Trump ‘peace plan’ report
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched missile strikes targeting U.S. military bases in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain, as well as Israeli positions. Crude oil prices fell sharply in early trading following reports of a Trump administration peace plan. An Iranian military spokesperson dismissed U.S. ceasefire efforts, saying Americans were negotiating only with themselves.

stories.title: Watchdog takes legal action against syndicate seeking ‘quarter of renovation market’
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Competition Commission launched legal proceedings against a syndicate accused of trying to control roughly a quarter of the building maintenance market. The case involves eight companies and 12 individuals across six undertakings, including a bid linked to a Tai Po housing complex hit by a deadly fire.

stories.title: Moldovan parliament backs energy state of emergency after power line knocked out of service
stories.summary: Moldova's parliament approved a 60-day energy state of emergency after Russian strikes on neighboring Ukraine disabled a power line that supplies most of Moldova's electricity.

stories.title: No Israel prosecutions for killing Palestinian civilians in occupied West Bank since start of decade
stories.summary: A Guardian analysis found that Israel has not prosecuted any of its citizens for killing Palestinian civilians in the occupied West Bank since the start of the decade. Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert called for International Criminal Court intervention. Dozens of former Israeli military and intelligence officials described the situation as 'organised Jewish terrorism.'

stories.title: Iran to allow 'non-hostile' ships through Hormuz, excludes US-linked vessels
stories.summary: Iran notified the International Maritime Organisation that it will permit "non-hostile" ships through the Strait of Hormuz but will exclude vessels linked to the United States, Israel, and other countries it accuses of aggression. The policy was outlined in a letter to member states.

stories.title: Nigeria: Switzerland to Return Benin Bronzes, Back Nigeria On Security
stories.summary: Switzerland and Nigeria agreed to return Benin Bronzes and strengthen bilateral relations spanning trade, security, and cultural exchange. The agreement also covers economic cooperation, skills acquisition, and migration issues.

stories.title: Nigeria: Switzerland to Return Benin Bronzes, Back Nigeria On Security
stories.summary: Nigeria and Switzerland agreed to strengthen bilateral relations across trade, security, migration, and cultural exchange. Switzerland also committed to returning Benin Bronzes to Nigeria.

stories.title: Liberia: Ex-Combatants Issue One-Week Ultimatum to Guinean Troops Amid Border Tensions
stories.summary: Former combatants in Nimba County, Liberia, issued a one-week ultimatum to Guinean troops reportedly occupying parts of Liberian territory near the Guinea border. The demand escalates tensions despite ongoing diplomatic efforts between the two countries.

stories.title: Liberia: Ex-Combatants Issue One-Week Ultimatum to Guinean Troops Amid Border Tensions
stories.summary: In Ganta, Nimba County, Liberia, former combatants issued a one-week ultimatum demanding that Guinean troops withdraw from areas they reportedly occupy along the Liberia-Guinea border, escalating tensions despite ongoing diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Parsi: No deal ‘’without both sides giving something to the other’
stories.summary: Analyst Trita Parsi argued that Iran is unlikely to agree to end the ongoing war without receiving sanctions relief in return. He emphasized that any deal would require concessions from both sides.

stories.title: Thousands march to mark 50th anniversary of Argentina’s bloody coup
stories.summary: Thousands of people marched through Buenos Aires to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Argentina's 1976 military coup, which ushered in a period of widespread repression and human rights abuses.

stories.title: New Zealand footballers willing to play Iran World Cup match outside US
stories.summary: New Zealand's football team has expressed willingness to play their FIFA World Cup match against Iran outside the United States. The June 15 match is scheduled for Los Angeles, but Iran has threatened to boycott due to the ongoing war.

stories.title: After decades, terror victims to receive proceeds from sale of Iran-linked NYC skyscraper
stories.summary: A Manhattan office tower linked to Iran is set to be sold as part of a $318 million settlement. Proceeds will compensate families of terror victims, including those killed in the 2001 Sbarro bombing in Jerusalem.

stories.title: Fars: Iranian child dies from 'psychological shock ' after explosion
stories.summary: A 10-year-old girl in the Iranian city of Yazd died from shock and psychological stress following an explosion linked to a strike on a nearby military site, according to Fars news agency.

stories.title: Israel’s military to occupy swathe of southern Lebanon amid widening war
stories.summary: Israel announced it will militarily occupy southern Lebanon up to the Litani River, approximately 30 kilometers north of the Israeli border. Defence Minister Israel Katz described the area as a "security zone," marking the first explicit declaration of intent to seize territory amounting to nearly one-tenth of Lebanon.

stories.title: China says disputes must be resolved through dialogue
stories.summary: China's foreign ministry called for dialogue to resolve Middle East tensions, urging all parties to pursue peace talks and de-escalation amid the ongoing regional conflict.

stories.title: Iranian missile attacks intensify over Israel after brief lull
stories.summary: Iranian missile attacks on Israel resumed after a brief lull, with air raid sirens sounding across central areas including Tel Aviv. In Bnei Brak, a missile struck a residential area, injuring nine people including six children.

stories.title: Sheriff who responded to Temple Israel attack faces online backlash
stories.summary: Oakland County Sheriff Mike Bouchard, who responded to an attack on Temple Israel, faced online backlash including antisemitic memes. Bouchard denounced the social media users, saying they use free speech as cover for antisemitism.

stories.title: Russia tries to blackmail Europe and world with 'little green men' – intelligence
stories.summary: Russia's State Duma received proposed amendments to citizenship and defense laws that would grant President Vladimir Putin authority to deploy military forces abroad to "protect" Russian citizens facing arrest or prosecution by foreign courts. Ukrainian intelligence characterized the move as blackmail against Europe.

stories.title: ABC strike: national broadcaster switches to BBC programming as staff walk off the job for 24 hours
stories.summary: More than 2,000 ABC staff across Australia walked off the job for a 24-hour strike, disrupting television, radio, and digital services. The broadcaster switched to BBC World Service and repeat programming. Managing director Hugh Marks said the ABC would not concede to workers' demands despite the disruption.

stories.title: Pope Leo laments that Iran war 'getting worse and worse'
stories.summary: Pope Leo voiced concern over the escalating Iran war, calling for a ceasefire. His remarks came amid reports that the United States is planning to deploy thousands of additional soldiers to the Middle East.

stories.title: Chad: Chad Relocates Refugees Amid Rising Tensions At Border With Sudan
stories.summary: Chad has begun emergency relocation of refugees from its border with Sudan as the army prepares to deploy in response to cross-border attacks. An official from Chad's refugee agency confirmed the operation.

stories.title: Chad: Chad Relocates Refugees Amid Rising Tensions At Border With Sudan
stories.summary: Chad began emergency relocation of refugees from its border with Sudan as the Chadian army prepared to deploy to the area in response to cross-border attacks, according to a national refugee agency official.

stories.title: East Africa: As East Africa's Migratory Fish Vanish, a Food Security Crisis Surfaces
stories.summary: Migratory fish populations in East Africa's Rufiji River and surrounding waterways are declining sharply, threatening food security in the region. At Tanzania's Nangurukuru fish market, catches have dropped dramatically, with key species like long-whiskered catfish disappearing.

stories.title: Sudan: Hospital Strike Highlights Surge in Drone Attacks On Civilians
stories.summary: The death toll from an attack on a hospital in Sudan's Darfur region has continued to rise. UN agencies reported a sharp increase in drone attacks targeting civilians in Sudan in 2025.

stories.title: East Africa: As East Africa's Migratory Fish Vanish, a Food Security Crisis Surfaces
stories.summary: Migratory fish populations in East Africa's Rufiji River and surrounding waters are declining sharply, threatening food security for communities in Tanzania and the broader region that depend on freshwater catches.

stories.title: Sudan: Hospital Strike Highlights Surge in Drone Attacks On Civilians
stories.summary: The UN reported a rising death toll from a drone attack on a hospital in Sudan's Darfur region, noting a sharp increase in drone strikes targeting civilians in 2024.

stories.title: Visa-free travel, rising foreign visitors boost luxury hotel growth in China
stories.summary: China's luxury hotel sector is experiencing growth driven by increased inbound tourism and visa-free travel policies. International visitors, mainly from developed countries, tend to spend more than domestic tourists. The trend has opened new revenue streams for high-end hospitality businesses across China.

stories.title: Kenya: Kenya's Double Climate Crisis - It Needs Funds to Adapt, and Disaster Aid Is Damaging the Environment
stories.summary: Kenya faces a dual climate crisis involving the need for adaptation funding and environmental damage caused by disaster aid itself. Extreme weather events including floods, mudslides, and droughts have caused trillions of dollars in economic losses over the past two decades.

stories.title: Kenya: Kenya's Double Climate Crisis - It Needs Funds to Adapt, and Disaster Aid Is Damaging the Environment
stories.summary: Kenya faces a compounding climate crisis as extreme weather events including floods, mudslides, and drought have caused trillions of dollars in economic losses over two decades, while disaster aid itself is contributing to environmental damage.

stories.title: Venezuelan man sues US over deportation to El Salvadoran prison
stories.summary: A Venezuelan man filed a lawsuit seeking at least $1.3 million in damages against the U.S. government, alleging he was wrongfully identified as a gang member and deported to a prison in El Salvador in violation of a U.S. court order.

stories.title: Canada tells Israel that Lebanon’s sovereignty ‘must not be violated’
stories.summary: Canada and France have called on Israel to halt preparations for an occupation of southern Lebanon, insisting that Lebanese sovereignty must be respected.

stories.title: Iran military spokesman rejects negotiation claims
stories.summary: Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya military headquarters rejected US claims of ongoing negotiations. Lieutenant Colonel Ebrahim Zolfaghari dismissed President Trump's statements, warning there would be no return to previous conditions.

stories.title: China’s 7-day hypersonic design; Andy Lau’s Ming mystery: 7 science highlights
stories.summary: Profiles of top Chinese nuclear, radar, and missile scientists—including radar specialist Wu Manqing—have been removed from the website of China's engineering academy. Separately, Chinese researchers reportedly completed a hypersonic vehicle design in seven days, highlighting advances in rapid military technology development.

stories.title: The Israeli-Iranian handshake at Pope John Paul II's funeral
stories.summary: At the 2005 funeral of Pope John Paul II in Vatican City, then-Israeli president Moshe Katsav and then-Iranian president Mohammad Khatami were seen shaking hands, following the customary protocol of greeting those seated nearby at major international gatherings.

stories.title: What we know about the US’s 15-point plan Iran proposal
stories.summary: US media reported that the Trump administration has proposed a temporary ceasefire and a 15-point plan to end the ongoing war with Iran, though details remain under discussion.

stories.title: Australia backs Lebanon’s sovereignty and opposes occupation, Penny Wong tells Israel
stories.summary: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong told her Israeli counterpart that Australia supports Lebanon's sovereignty and opposes Israeli occupation of southern Lebanon. Wong also reiterated Australia's condemnation of Iran over the Strait of Hormuz closure. The statement followed Israel's announcement of plans for a defensive buffer zone in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Two dead in school shooting in western Mexico; teenager arrested
stories.summary: A 15-year-old boy was arrested after allegedly shooting and killing two female staff members, including a teacher, at a private school in the western Mexican state of Michoacán, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Colombia seeks arrest of rebel leaders over 2025 assassination of senator
stories.summary: Colombia's attorney general issued arrest warrants for the top leaders of the Segunda Marquetalia rebel group in connection with the 2025 assassination of senator and presidential hopeful Miguel Uribe.

stories.title: What Are the Laws of War Good For?
stories.summary: An analysis argues that U.S. Secretary of Defense fails to grasp how the laws of war and rules of engagement serve the strategic interests of the American military. The piece examines the utility of international humanitarian law for U.S. forces.

stories.title: Nasa abandons orbital station, plans moon base and nuclear spacecraft
stories.summary: NASA cancelled its planned lunar orbital space station and will instead redirect components toward building a roughly $20 billion base on the moon's surface. Administrator Jared Isaacman, appointed by President Trump, also announced plans to send a nuclear-powered spacecraft to Mars as part of a restructured Artemis program.

stories.title: BTS fans fume over Jin’s absence from ‘Arirang’ credits
stories.summary: BTS member Jin's absence from the production credits of the group's new album "Arirang" sparked fan debate. During a live broadcast celebrating the album's release, member RM acknowledged that Jin's ongoing tour schedule may have limited his involvement in the recording process.

stories.title: US to send thousands of soldiers from 82nd Airborne Division to Middle East
stories.summary: The United States is expected to deploy up to 3,000 troops from the 82nd Airborne Division to the Middle East amid the ongoing conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Trump’s approval rating further sinks as fuel prices surge amid Iran war — poll
stories.summary: A Reuters/Ipsos poll found President Trump's approval rating fell to 36 percent, the lowest since his return to the White House, as fuel prices surged amid the war with Iran.

stories.title: Iran says 'non-hostile' ships can transit Strait of Hormuz, FT reports
stories.summary: Iran informed International Maritime Organization member states that non-hostile vessels may transit the Strait of Hormuz if they coordinate with Iranian authorities, according to a letter reported by the Financial Times.

stories.title: Iran says ‘non-hostile’ ships can pass safely through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran informed the International Maritime Organisation that it will allow "non-hostile" ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. The announcement came as President Trump indicated talks were under way to end the war.

stories.title: Drone attack ignites fuel tank at Kuwait airport
stories.summary: A drone attack ignited a fuel tank at Kuwait International Airport, sparking a fire at the facility.

stories.title: Canada 'strongly condemns' Israeli plan to occupy buffer zone in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Canada strongly condemned Israel's plan to occupy a buffer zone in southern Lebanon between the Litani River and Israel's northern border. The plan is aimed at reducing threats posed by Hezbollah.

stories.title: IRGC says new strikes mark 'beginning of targeting' Israeli forces in Gaza
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced a new wave of attacks under Operation "True Promise 4," stating the strikes targeted Israeli military sites and marked the beginning of targeting Israeli forces in Gaza and northern Palestine.

stories.title: Middle East live: Israeli strikes on South Lebanon leave nine dead
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon killed at least nine people, hitting a town and a Palestinian refugee camp near Sidon. The strikes occurred as President Donald Trump expressed optimism about ending the conflict after sending a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran.

stories.title: Avraham Burg, longtime fixture of Israeli left, meets Tucker Carlson on his own turf
stories.summary: Former Israeli Knesset Speaker Avraham Burg, a prominent figure on the Israeli left, appeared in a video interview with American commentator Tucker Carlson. Burg opened the exchange by telling Carlson he could not stand him but acknowledged him as a nice person.

stories.title: Naftogaz discusses increasing U.S. LNG purchases with American delegation
stories.summary: Ukrainian state energy company Naftogaz met with a U.S. delegation from the Treasury Department and the International Development Finance Corporation, along with U.S. Chargé d'Affaires Julie S. Davis, to discuss increasing Ukraine's purchases of American liquefied natural gas.

stories.title: Sara Duterte impeachment hearings start as political death match heats up
stories.summary: The Philippine House of Representatives opened new impeachment hearings against Vice President Sara Duterte, with her potential 2028 presidential bid at stake as the political confrontation with the Marcos administration intensifies.

stories.title: Danish left-wing bloc leads election, lacks majority, exit polls show
stories.summary: Exit polls from Denmark's election showed the left-wing bloc leading but neither the left nor the right expected to secure a majority of parliamentary seats.

stories.title: Trump says 'this war has been won' as Iran denies any agreement
stories.summary: President Trump declared "this war has been won," claiming the US-Israel campaign eliminated key Iranian leaders and secured commitments from Tehran against pursuing nuclear weapons. Iran denied any negotiations or agreement.

stories.title: Journalists at Australia's national broadcaster strike for first time in 20 years
stories.summary: Journalists at Australia's national broadcaster, the ABC, walked out on a 24-hour strike—the first in 20 years—over a pay rise offer that fell below the rate of inflation.

stories.title: The Maga divide over Iran – podcast
stories.summary: Guardian global affairs correspondent Andrew Roth discussed the U.S. and Israeli war on Iran in a podcast, noting the conflict's unpopularity among the American public. He highlighted divisions within the MAGA movement over the war and the lack of a clear long-term military strategy.

stories.title: Shell CEO says fuel shortages may reach Europe next month
stories.summary: Shell CEO Wael Sawan warned that fuel shortages could reach Europe within a month if the war involving Iran continues. He noted shortages have already affected parts of Asia and urged governments to strengthen energy supply resilience.

stories.title: French tycoon Bollore denies political war against public broadcaster
stories.summary: French media tycoon Vincent Bolloré testified before lawmakers in Paris, denying accusations that his conservative media empire is waging a political war against public broadcasting. He called himself a scapegoat for a hostile elite.

stories.title: Top US official does not rule out resuming underground nuclear weapons tests
stories.summary: A senior U.S. State Department official said Washington is still assessing how to implement President Trump's order to resume nuclear weapons testing and did not rule out full-scale underground explosive tests.

stories.title: Trump says Iran made a major energy-related gift to the US
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that Iran had made a major energy-related concession to the United States, calling it a positive development, but provided no specific details.

stories.title: Terrorist attack in Bucha: Police notify perpetrator of suspicion
stories.summary: Ukrainian police formally notified a 21-year-old Bucha resident of suspicion in connection with a terrorist act committed in the Kyiv-region city.

stories.title: Israeli victims of Iranian terrorism among those to be compensated after sale of NYC skyscraper
stories.summary: Israeli victims of Iranian-linked terrorism are expected to receive compensation from the sale of a New York City skyscraper at 650 Fifth Avenue. The US government first moved to seize the building in 2008 after discovering a secret ownership stake held by an Iranian government-owned bank.

stories.title: Denmark's Frederiksen weakened by election setback, coalition talks loom
stories.summary: Denmark's Social Democrats, led by Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, won the most seats in Tuesday's general election but recorded their weakest result in over 120 years. The left-wing bloc failed to secure a parliamentary majority, setting the stage for coalition negotiations.

stories.title: Turkey’s biggest private bank plans Hong Kong entry amid Middle East tensions: sources
stories.summary: Türkiye İş Bankası, Turkey's largest private bank, plans to open an office in Hong Kong after its board approved the expansion two months ago. The lender is awaiting clearance from Turkish authorities before applying to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority for a banking licence, aiming to connect China and Asian markets with the Middle East.

stories.title: Iraqi militia group claims 23 operations targeting 'enemy bases'
stories.summary: The Islamic Resistance in Iraq claimed 23 operations targeting "enemy bases" in Iraq and across the region over 24 hours, using dozens of drones and missiles. The network includes factions such as Kataib Hezbollah.

stories.title: Washington's proposal to Iran outlines nuclear rollback, US media says
stories.summary: US media reported that Washington sent Iran a 15-point plan calling for dismantlement of main nuclear sites, a halt to uranium enrichment, suspension of its ballistic missile program, and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. In return, the US would lift nuclear-related sanctions.

stories.title: In Broadway’s ‘Giant,’ Roald Dahl is a warped messenger for a vital debate about Israel
stories.summary: A new Broadway play titled "Giant," starring John Lithgow, portrays children's author Roald Dahl and explores his antisemitic statements. The production examines themes relevant to contemporary debates about Israel in the Jewish Diaspora.

stories.title: Gulf warnings and fears of miscalculation preceded Trump’s pause in Iran showdown
stories.summary: Gulf states warned the U.S. that its confrontation with Iran was entering a more dangerous phase, with regional officials fearing Washington had underestimated Tehran's willingness to escalate, according to regional sources. The warnings preceded Trump's abrupt pause in the standoff.

stories.title: Air strike hits Tehran as missile intercepted in central Israel
stories.summary: An airstrike hit a residential area in Tehran, with rescue teams searching for survivors. Separately, Israeli authorities said a missile launched from Iran was intercepted over central Israel, with no casualties reported from the interception.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s CK Hutchison expands Panama ports claim as losses ‘surpass’ US$2 billion
stories.summary: CK Hutchison Holdings' subsidiary Panama Ports Company has expanded its international arbitration claims against Panama, alleging damages exceeding $2 billion from what it called an illegal government takeover. Panamanian authorities had seized control of terminals at the ports of Balboa and Cristóbal roughly a month earlier.

stories.title: Report: Trump does not rule out troop deployment in Iran, seizing Kharg Island
stories.summary: The Washington Post reported that President Trump has not ruled out deploying US ground troops to Iran. Options under consideration include seizing Kharg Island, a key Iranian oil export hub, though no deployment order has been issued.

stories.title: Ghana's president, in New York, says US 'normalising' erasure of Black history
stories.summary: Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama, speaking in New York, criticized the U.S. administration for what he described as normalizing the erasure of Black history and warned such policies could have broader international consequences.

stories.title: Kuwait responding to missile and drone attacks, military says
stories.summary: Kuwait's military said it is responding to missile and drone attacks, with air defenses intercepting incoming threats. The National Guard shot down five drones, while a separate drone strike caused a fire at a fuel tank at Kuwait International Airport.

stories.title: Venezuela opposition leader Maria Corina Machado pushes for energy investment security, transparency
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, speaking in Houston, welcomed early interest in Venezuela's oil sector but called for greater transparency, contract security, and a new oil law to boost crude and gas production.

stories.title: World gave Israel 'licence to torture Palestinians': Albanese
stories.summary: UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese accused the international community of giving Israel a "licence to torture Palestinians," describing Israel's use of torture as state policy in the occupied Palestinian territories.

stories.title: Decades after Romania’s secret police trailed a Jewish photographer, their files have become a film
stories.summary: The documentary "Plan contraplan/Shot Reverse Shot," which premiered at the Berlinale film festival, explores the experiences of Jewish photojournalist Edward Serotta in 1980s Romania, drawing on secret police surveillance files from that era.

stories.title: Can Taiwan fulfil its Asia-Pacific drone hub goal with a ‘non-red’ supply chain push?
stories.summary: Taiwan is pursuing a strategy to become an Asia-Pacific drone manufacturing hub by building supply chains decoupled from mainland China. President William Lai Ching-te's administration is promoting a "democratic supply chain" free of Chinese components. Experts note challenges related to scale, political dynamics, and timing.

stories.title: How ‘salmon’ raised in landlocked Xinjiang is netting fans in China
stories.summary: An emerging trout-farming industry is developing in China's landlocked Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region, using meltwater from snow-capped mountains. The region, traditionally known for cotton, is on track to become China's top trout producer as it diversifies agriculture following international cotton import bans over labour practice concerns.

stories.title: US expected to send thousands more soldiers to Middle East, sources say
stories.summary: The Pentagon is expected to deploy thousands of soldiers from the U.S. Army's 82nd Airborne Division to the Middle East, adding to a significant military buildup even as President Trump discusses a possible deal with Tehran to end the conflict.

stories.title: Court blocks California effort to stop Republican sheriff’s ballot recount
stories.summary: A three-judge panel in California denied Attorney General Rob Bonta's request for a court order to stop Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco's department from recounting approximately 650,000 ballots from the November 2025 special election. Bonta argued the sheriff's investigation threatened public confidence in elections.

stories.title: Three US and Czech citizens detained over arson attack on Czech arms producer
stories.summary: Czech police detained three individuals — holding U.S. and Czech citizenship — in connection with an arson attack on a Czech arms producer. Authorities did not specify the exact nationalities of the detainees.

stories.title: Philippine president declares energy emergency as impact of Iran war felt
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. declared an energy emergency as the war involving Iran disrupted fuel supplies. Transport unions criticized the declaration as a superficial measure that fails to address the root causes of the crisis.

stories.title: US notified Israel before presenting Iran with Trump’s conditions for ending war — official
stories.summary: A US official said Washington notified Israel before presenting Iran with President Trump's conditions for ending the war. Separately, no direct injuries were reported from overnight Iranian missile attacks on Israel.

stories.title: China consumer stocks jump on strong earnings, but analysts warn of limited recovery
stories.summary: Major Chinese consumer stocks listed in Hong Kong rose after strong annual earnings. Jeweller Laopu Gold reported revenues of 27.3 billion yuan with a 221 percent year-on-year surge, and net profit jumped nearly 235 percent. However, analysts cautioned that results reflected structural divergence rather than a broad consumer recovery.

stories.title: Philippines declares national emergency as fuel supplies dwindle
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. declared a year-long national emergency as fuel supplies dwindled due to disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Indian police manage long lines as panic grows over fuel shortages
stories.summary: Indian police were stationed at petrol pumps in Gujarat state as public panic grew over potential fuel shortages linked to the broader energy disruptions from the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Oh deer: famous hoofed residents of Japan’s Nara wander as far as Osaka
stories.summary: Sacred deer from Nara, Japan, are increasingly wandering far from their traditional habitat in the city's famous park. A male deer was recently spotted in Osaka's Zengenji district, roughly 40 kilometers away. The sightings in urban areas have drawn crowds of onlookers.

stories.title: Zaluzhnyi now blames Zelenskyy for the counteroffensive. He wasn’t always so sure.
stories.summary: Former Ukrainian commander-in-chief Valerii Zaluzhnyi has blamed President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for the 2023 counteroffensive, which encountered heavily fortified Russian defensive lines without adequate air cover. The article notes an ongoing blame game among Kyiv's leadership.

stories.title: Zhytomyr resident sentenced to 15 years for leaking Ukrainian aircraft data to Russia
stories.summary: A resident of Ukraine's Zhytomyr region was sentenced to 15 years in prison for providing Russian intelligence services with information about the movements of Ukrainian Armed Forces aircraft.

stories.title: Nine people wounded in Bnei Brak by Iranian cluster bomb munitions
stories.summary: Nine people were wounded in Bnei Brak, Israel, by Iranian cluster bomb munitions as Iran fired 13 salvos throughout Tuesday. The IDF said it struck a main explosives facility near Isfahan, while Tehran accused the US and Israel of bombing the Bushehr nuclear site.

stories.title: ​Cowardly bully: On Donald Trump and the Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump faces criticism over the ongoing war involving Iran, with calls for him to end hostilities and pressure Israel to cease its operations against Iran.

stories.title: Israeli and Palestinian mothers call for peace on barefoot walk
stories.summary: Israeli and Palestinian mothers marched barefoot through Rome, calling for peace and greater protection for children affected by the conflict.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill nine in Lebanon's south
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed nine people in southern Lebanon as Israel escalated attacks across the country and pushed forward with its ground invasion in the south.

stories.title: Iran tells UN: 'non-hostile' ships can transit Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran sent a note to the UN Security Council and Secretary-General António Guterres stating that "non-hostile" ships would be permitted to transit the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Trump’s approval hits new 36% low as fuel prices surge amid Iran war, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
stories.summary: A Reuters/Ipsos poll found President Trump's approval rating has dropped to a new low of 36 per cent. The decline is attributed to surging fuel prices and widespread disapproval of the U.S. war on Iran.

stories.title: Gangs tighten grip on Haiti despite more aggressive policing, UN report finds
stories.summary: A United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights report released Tuesday found that one in four Haitians live in areas controlled by criminal gangs. Despite more aggressive policing, armed groups have continued to consolidate their control across large parts of the Caribbean island nation.

stories.title: Oil drops over 5% after Trump proposes talks with Iran
stories.summary: Oil prices dropped more than 5 percent after President Trump sent a delegation to Iran, raising hopes of ending the conflict. Brent crude fell nearly 6 percent to $98.30, and Iran signaled it would allow non-hostile vessels through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Paris offices of Swiss bank Edmond de Rothschild raided in Epstein-linked probe into diplomat
stories.summary: French authorities raided the Paris offices of Swiss bank Edmond de Rothschild as part of a probe linked to Jeffrey Epstein. Diplomat Fabrice Aidan is alleged to have sent confidential information and documents to Epstein.

stories.title: Denmark's Frederiksen weakened by election setback, coalition talks loom
stories.summary: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's Social Democrats suffered a significant electoral setback, trending toward their worst result in over a century. Despite international support for her stance on Greenland against Washington, domestic concerns over migration and cost of living dominated the vote.

stories.title: Philippines declares state of national emergency amid energy disruptions
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. declared a year-long state of national energy emergency, citing imminent danger to the country's energy supply. The measure aims to address disruptions caused by the Middle East conflict and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: A missile launch pad on the seabed? Chinese simulation suggests it’s possible
stories.summary: Chinese scientists demonstrated that a solid rocket engine can ignite at 200 meters underwater, significantly deeper than current submarine-launched missile systems. The test results suggest new possibilities for deep-sea weapon launch platforms, potentially expanding strategic deterrence capabilities beyond conventional submarine-based systems.

stories.title: ‘Be careful or I’ll kill your family’: China mini-dramas featuring kids raise concerns
stories.summary: Chinese mini-dramas starring children have drawn criticism for featuring adult-oriented content, including depictions of a five-year-old making stock investments yielding billions of yuan. Critics and the China Youth Daily warn that such "adultified" roles could harm young actors' psychological health.

stories.title: Missile debris lands south of Amman, no injuries reported
stories.summary: Jordanian authorities reported that missile shrapnel fell in a sparsely populated area south of Amman, with no injuries or significant damage. Officials noted hundreds of missile debris incidents across Jordan since the war began on February 28.

stories.title: More young people want to vote in New Zealand’s Māori electorates. What are they and how do they work?
stories.summary: New data from New Zealand's electoral commission shows growing registration among young voters for the Māori electoral roll, with 58 percent of eligible 18- to 24-year-olds signed up, compared to 50 percent in 2023. The increase comes ahead of November elections and after years of strained relations between Indigenous communities and the coalition government.

stories.title: Saudi air defences destroy missile, drones in Eastern Province
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia intercepted a ballistic missile and three drones over the Eastern Province as part of efforts to protect its airspace and critical infrastructure. Defense officials said threats were destroyed before reaching their targets.

stories.title: Several injured as Karachi-bound Tezgam Express derails near Punjab’s Lodhran: official
stories.summary: The Karachi-bound Tezgam Express derailed near Lodhran in Punjab, Pakistan, on Tuesday night. At least 17 people received first aid on site, while eight others were hospitalized. Pakistan Railways reported no fatalities and said a high-level inquiry had been ordered.

stories.title: Sirens sound in north Israel after projectile from Lebanon
stories.summary: Air raid sirens sounded in Kiryat Shmona and nearby areas in northern Israel after a projectile was launched from Lebanon. A house under construction was damaged, but no casualties were reported.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Trump says Iran gave U.S. 'very big present' related to oil and gas
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated on Tuesday that negotiations with Iran to end the Middle East war were actively underway. He claimed Tehran was eager to reach a deal and had offered the U.S. a significant concession related to oil and gas.

stories.title: Clerics from Pakistan, Afghanistan appeal to authorities to extend pause in fighting till Eidul Azha
stories.summary: A group of clerics from Pakistan and Afghanistan called on authorities in both countries to extend the pause in hostilities, originally announced for Eidul Fitr, through Eidul Azha. Pakistan's government had initially declared the pause on March 18 at the request of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey.

stories.title: Russia uses migration pressure to recruit foreigners into its army – Ukrainian intelligence
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence reported that Moscow has developed a mechanism to coerce foreigners into Russian military service by exploiting migration pressures, while avoiding direct recruitment practices.

stories.title: Avraham Burg, longtime fixture of Israeli left, meets Tucker Carlson on his own turf
stories.summary: Former Israeli politician Avraham Burg, a figure associated with the Israeli left, appeared in an interview with right-wing commentator Tucker Carlson. The meeting reflects how some progressive Israelis are engaging with voices on the political right.

stories.title: Trump says he received Iranian 'present' as thousands of US troops head towards Gulf
stories.summary: President Trump said Iran gave the US a "present" related to oil and gas while claiming talks were under way with Tehran. Meanwhile, thousands of US troops are being deployed toward the Gulf region.

stories.title: Cathay’s European flights could offset Middle East losses, experts say
stories.summary: Cathay Pacific Airways suspended Middle Eastern flights due to the ongoing regional conflict, but aviation experts say expanded European services should offset passenger revenue losses. Analysts warned of broader impacts on cargo operations, as the Middle East served as a cost-effective transit route, with rising fuel and insurance costs adding further pressure.

stories.title: Philippines declares ‘national energy emergency’ and boosts coal power as Iran war grinds on
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos declared a year-long national energy emergency citing the Middle East war's threat to fuel supplies. The declaration empowers officials to address fuel hoarding and profiteering. The country's energy secretary announced plans to increase coal-fired power output to compensate for potential supply shortfalls.

stories.title: Lula warns he will not allow others to seize Brazil's critical minerals
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva declared he would not allow other countries to seize Brazil's rare earths and critical minerals. The remarks were widely interpreted as a warning directed at the United States amid a growing bilateral dispute over control of strategic resources.

stories.title: Reacher star Alan Ritchson acted in self-defense in neighbor fight, Tennessee police say
stories.summary: Tennessee police concluded that actor Alan Ritchson, star of the TV series Reacher, acted in self-defense during a violent confrontation with neighbor Ronnie Taylor. Video obtained by TMZ showed Ritchson striking Taylor in a suburban Tennessee neighborhood. No criminal charges will be filed against either party.

stories.title: Venezuela sends diplomatic delegation to Washington to formalize restoration of ties with US
stories.summary: Venezuela's acting president Delcy Rodríguez announced that a diplomatic delegation would travel to Washington to advance normalization of bilateral relations with the United States. Diplomatic ties between the two countries were severed in 2019.

stories.title: US proposes 15-point plan as Iran opens Hormuz to 'non-hostile' oil vessels
stories.summary: President Donald Trump sent a 15-point peace plan to Iran amid nearly a month of hostilities, expressing cautious optimism about ending the conflict. In a potential de-escalation signal, Tehran announced it would permit passage of 'non-hostile' vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global oil shipping route.

stories.title: Rights group exposes North Korea’s forced labour scheme that reaps US$500 million annually
stories.summary: Global Rights Compliance published a report revealing that a North Korean state-sponsored forced labour programme generates up to $500 million annually. The report, containing first-hand testimonies, details workers subjected to control, abuse, and coercion under conditions the rights group described as brutal.

stories.title: Modi, Dissanayake discuss ‘energy cooperation’ over telephone call
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake spoke by telephone to discuss energy cooperation. The two leaders also addressed the ongoing war in West Asia and its impact on global supply chains.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump again says talks under way; 12 killed in south Tehran
stories.summary: US-Israeli airstrikes on Iran continued despite President Trump's claims that negotiations were under way. At least 12 people were killed and 28 wounded in a single attack on southern Tehran.

stories.title: Fallout from Iranian strike on Dimona plant would be symbolic, not radioactive
stories.summary: Experts said an Iranian missile strike near Israel's Dimona nuclear facility would carry symbolic rather than radiological significance. Analysts assessed that a hit on the reactor would pose little risk of contamination or nuclear explosion.

stories.title: Indra teams up with Hanwha for Spain’s $5.3 billion artillery order
stories.summary: Spain's Indra signed a binding agreement with South Korea's Hanwha to jointly produce 280 tracked vehicles based on Hanwha's K9 155mm self-propelled howitzer. The deal is part of Spain's approximately $5.3 billion artillery procurement program.

stories.title: Russian drone strike on Ivano-Frankivsk: Two dead, injury toll rises to six
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike on the city of Ivano-Frankivsk in western Ukraine on March 24 killed two people and injured six others, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Denmark faces weeks of coalition talks as Frederiksen emerges bruised in election
stories.summary: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's Social Democrats were headed for their worst election result in over a century, despite broad public support for her stance against Washington over Greenland. Migration and welfare concerns dominated the campaign. Weeks of coalition negotiations are expected as no bloc secured a clear majority.

stories.title: Tiltrotor who? US military helicopter deliveries rose 13 percent in 2025
stories.summary: The three major U.S. military helicopter manufacturers increased rotorcraft deliveries by 13 percent in 2025 compared to 2024. The growth came despite ongoing challenges in tiltrotor aircraft programs.

stories.title: Bahrain pushes UN-backed action for Hormuz shipping
stories.summary: Bahrain put forward a resolution at the UN Security Council addressing shipping safety in the Strait of Hormuz. France also presented a separate resolution, as the council debated measures to protect maritime transit through the vital waterway.

stories.title: Thousands march in Buenos Aires on 50th anniversary of military coup under "Never Again" banner
stories.summary: Tens of thousands marched in Buenos Aires on Tuesday to mark the 50th anniversary of the 1976 military coup that installed Argentina's last dictatorship. The commemoration was marked by tensions between the human rights movement and President Javier Milei's government over how the era is remembered.

stories.title: Russian weapons, tactics seen in Ukraine are shaping Myanmar’s civil war
stories.summary: Russian-supplied aircraft and tactics, including wave-style infantry assaults previously seen in Ukraine, are reportedly influencing the conduct of Myanmar's civil war by the country's military.

stories.title: Israeli military warns of inbound missiles from Iran, says anti-missile defences active
stories.summary: Israel's military warned late Tuesday that Iran had launched a new salvo of missiles toward the country, activating anti-missile defenses after more than a dozen alerts during the day. Sirens sounded in Jerusalem and explosions were heard there and over the West Bank city of Jericho.

stories.title: US deploys 82nd Airborne troops to the Gulf as Trump claims Iran offered a "gift"
stories.summary: The Pentagon is deploying soldiers from the 82nd Airborne Division to the Middle East amid the ongoing Iran conflict. President Trump simultaneously claimed negotiations with Iran were progressing and that Tehran had offered a "gift" related to gas, oil, and the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: EU ‘concerned’ by reports Hungary’s foreign minister leaked information to Russia
stories.summary: The European Union expressed concern over reports that Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó regularly called Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov to pass on information. The allegations raise questions about potential intelligence leaks within EU diplomatic circles.

stories.title: Danish PM’s leftwing bloc wins most votes but fails to secure majority – Europe live
stories.summary: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's left-leaning red bloc won 84 seats in the election, while the blue bloc secured 77 and the centrist Moderates took 14. Neither major bloc achieved an outright majority, pointing to extended coalition negotiations. The far-right Danish People's Party campaigned on fuel price concerns.

stories.title: Italy allocates EUR 45M to support war-affected Ukrainians
stories.summary: Italy allocated 45 million euros to support vulnerable populations in war-affected regions of Ukraine. An event marking the launch of the Italian-funded program was held in Kyiv.

stories.title: Board of Peace envoy lays out principles of disarmament plan presented to Hamas
stories.summary: UN Peace envoy Mladenov outlined principles of a phased disarmament plan presented to Hamas, urging the UN Security Council to support it. He also warned Israel that further military control of Gaza would not bring lasting security.

stories.title: US sent Iran 15-point proposal for ending war in Middle East - report
stories.summary: The United States reportedly sent Iran a 15-point proposal for ending the war, delivered via Pakistan. The plan addresses Iran's ballistic missile and nuclear programs as well as the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: War Diary Day 25: Pause holds but conflict’s underlying dynamics point to widening of scope
stories.summary: On day 25 of the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, Israeli strikes continued targeting energy and military infrastructure in Isfahan, Khorramshahr, and Tehran. President Trump's five-day pause on strikes against Iranian energy facilities provided limited respite, with the conflict's scope continuing to widen.

stories.title: The National Security Council is missing in action
stories.summary: An analysis highlights the Trump administration's National Security Council as largely absent during the war on Iran. The piece argues that the lack of a consistent strategic rationale for the conflict underscores the need for a properly functioning NSC.

stories.title: Trump keeps up claims of talks with ‘the right people’ in Iran
stories.summary: President Trump claimed talks with "the right people" in Iran were under way, though Israel appeared not to be aligned with the reported backchannel efforts and US military buildup in the region continued.

stories.title: Germany says two people arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia
stories.summary: German prosecutors announced on Tuesday that two individuals were arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia. The suspects allegedly gathered intelligence on a person who was supplying drones and related components to Ukraine.

stories.title: Man who talked down hospital bomber says would-be attacker asked for a cuddle
stories.summary: Nathan Newby, a hospital patient in the UK, persuaded Mohammad Farooq not to detonate a bomb in a maternity wing by engaging him calmly, with the would-be attacker ultimately asking for a cuddle before standing down. Newby is set to receive the George Medal for bravery for preventing the potential atrocity.

stories.title: Germany detains two Russian agents spying on supplier of drones for Ukraine
stories.summary: German federal prosecutors detained a Romanian woman and a Ukrainian man on suspicion of spying for a Russian intelligence service. The pair allegedly gathered information and filmed a person involved in supplying drones and drone components to Ukraine.

stories.title: UK police probe attack on Jewish ambulances
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police pledged to deploy 250 additional officers to patrol Jewish communities after an attack on Jewish ambulances. An investigation into the incident is under way.

stories.title: US unlikely to get China to join new nuclear arms control agreement, say experts
stories.summary: Experts said the United States is unlikely to persuade China to join a new nuclear arms control agreement in the near term, despite the Trump administration's push for a trilateral deal involving China and Russia after the previous US-Russia treaty expired.

stories.title: China is mapping the ocean floor as it prepares for submarine warfare with the U.S.
stories.summary: China is deploying research vessels to systematically map the ocean floor, navigating in tight survey lines to gather detailed underwater terrain data. The effort is linked to preparations for potential submarine warfare with the United States.

stories.title: Explosion, fire at Erbil high-rise amid Iranian attacks
stories.summary: Video footage showed a large explosion and fire at a high-rise building in Erbil, in Iraq's Kurdistan region, reportedly near the US Consulate, amid ongoing Iranian attacks.

stories.title: Australia politics live: NSW to compel oil companies to explain where extra petrol being sent; Rio Tinto aluminium smelter gets $2bn bailout
stories.summary: The Australian and Queensland governments announced a combined 2 billion Australian dollars in funding for Rio Tinto's Boyne aluminium smelter in central Queensland to ensure its long-term viability, with the investment expected to unlock approximately A$7.5 billion in private spending.

stories.title: Lockheed launches Hellfire missile from 10-foot cargo container
stories.summary: Lockheed Martin successfully launched a Hellfire missile from its containerized Grizzly launcher, a compact system housed in a 10-foot cargo container designed to provide a deployable and concealable strike capability.

stories.title: Lviv drone strike: 26 victims hospitalized
stories.summary: Twenty-six people injured during a Russian drone attack on the western Ukrainian city of Lviv on March 24 remain hospitalized. The strike was part of Russia's broader aerial campaign against Ukrainian cities.

stories.title: ‘Retarded Moroccan’: Senior Netanyahu aide under fire for reported racist tirades
stories.summary: Ziv Agmon, a senior aide to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, is facing calls for dismissal after reports that he used racist language against Sephardic Likud members of Knesset, allegedly calling them slurs. Agmon has denied wrongdoing, claiming an injustice was done to him.

stories.title: Lithuania warned in 2019 that Hungary posed NATO and EU leak risk, Poland says
stories.summary: Poland disclosed that Lithuania warned in 2019 that Hungary posed a leak risk to both NATO and the EU. Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó allegedly briefed Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov during breaks at EU meetings.

stories.title: Palestinian refugees in Lebanon face another forced displacement
stories.summary: Palestinian refugee Dalal Dawali was displaced from Beirut's southern suburb of Dahiyeh after Israeli bombing and fled to Beddawi camp in northern Lebanon, highlighting the repeated forced displacement faced by Palestinian refugees in the country.

stories.title: US officials downplay controller ‘distraction’ in New York LaGuardia plane crash
stories.summary: US officials downplayed reports that distracted air traffic controllers may have contributed to a fatal collision between an Air Canada jet and a fire truck at New York's LaGuardia Airport. Two pilots were killed when the plane's cockpit was crushed in the runway crash on Sunday.

stories.title: Russia fires nearly 400 drones at Ukraine with signs its spring offensive has started
stories.summary: Russia launched nearly 400 drones at Ukraine in a major escalation that may signal the start of a long-anticipated spring ground offensive. Moscow's forces intensified efforts to breach Ukrainian front-line defenses across the front.

stories.title: Two more people arrested over alleged Sydney kidnapping and murder of Chris Baghsarian
stories.summary: New South Wales police arrested two more people in connection with the alleged kidnapping and murder of Sydney grandfather Chris Baghsarian. Officers executed a search warrant in the suburb of Seven Hills, bringing in a man and a woman for questioning.

stories.title: Zelensky on massive attack: Russia not seeking to end war, more pressure needed
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russia's massive ongoing drone attacks, which have injured more than 40 people including five children, demonstrate that Moscow is not seeking to end the war. He called for increased pressure on Russia.

stories.title: Former IRGC commander Mohhammad Baqer Zolqadr named Iran’s new security chief
stories.summary: Former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Mohammad Baqer Zolqadr has been appointed Iran's new security chief. Zolqadr, who served as secretary of the Expediency Discernment Council, replaces Ali Larijani in the role.

stories.title: Deadly Iran school strike casts shadow over Pentagon’s AI targeting push
stories.summary: A deadly strike on a school in Minab, Iran, has raised questions about the Pentagon's push for AI-assisted targeting systems. A Ukrainian drone developer said the incident highlighted the risks inherent in semi-autonomous warfare.

stories.title: Afghanistan announces release of detained US linguist Dennis Coyle
stories.summary: Afghanistan announced the release of detained U.S. linguist Dennis Coyle. The family of the last Afghan detainee held at Guantánamo Bay is seeking a reciprocal release in connection with the case.

stories.title: Strikes hit Iran, Tehran targets Israel and Gulf states amid mixed signals over talks to end war
stories.summary: Strikes continued to hit targets in Iran while Tehran launched attacks against Israel and Gulf states, amid conflicting signals over potential peace talks. Uncertainty persists over who in Iran's government holds the authority or willingness to negotiate, especially after Israel killed several senior leaders.

stories.title: Meta ordered to pay US$375 million in New Mexico child safety trial
stories.summary: A New Mexico jury found Meta liable for endangering children on Facebook and Instagram by making them vulnerable to predators, sexual abuse, and online solicitation. After roughly a day of deliberations following a six-week trial, the jury awarded $375 million in damages, less than the state's requested $2.2 billion.

stories.title: Hungary is 'the Kremlin's biggest agent in the EU', analyst says
stories.summary: Dr. Mark Loustau of the Central European University described Hungary as the Kremlin's largest agent within the European Union, citing Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's efforts to destabilize EU unity and undermine Ukraine. Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó is alleged to have leaked sensitive EU negotiation details to Russia.
